title: Senior Full Stack Product Engineer (TypeScript)
location: Canada,  Ireland,  Netherlands,  Portugal,  Spain,  UK
description:
About Maze 

Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development. 

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey —and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values .

Location: Remote , preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales. 

The Role 

As a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer on the Product Engineering team, you'll design and deliver high impact features, working closely with product, design, and other engineers to solve complex problems, build scalable solutions, and ensure our systems are maintainable and performant.

You’ll take ownership of projects from concept to production, contribute to architectural decisions, write high quality code, and help raise the technical bar by sharing knowledge and best practices with your teammates.

You'll work on:

- 
Building elegant features for user researchers to analyze and extract compelling insights from qualitative data, using both classical techniques and large language models 

- 
Expanding audience management to help researchers connect with and reward participants from across the world

- 
Integrating video and scheduling tools to provide a streamlined experience for managing and booking user interviews

As a product engineer at Maze, you will:

- 
Partner closely with product managers, designers and other engineers to design, build, and ship new features

- 
Establish best practices, frameworks, and repeatable processes that enable us to measure the impact of every feature that we ship 

- 
Evaluate and improve the performance, maintainability, and security of applications in production

- 
Work in a collaborative and open team, which places high value on feedback, continuous learning and trust.

You should apply if:

- 
You're proficient with modern full-stack JavaScript (Node.js and React) and relational databases (PostgreSQL)

- 
You're enthusiastic about well-tested code and strive to improve your work environment

- 
You have excellent written and spoken English skills

- 
You thrive in a remote environment

Bonus points:

- 
You have Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, and/or TypeScript experience

- 
You have experience with AWS and/or Kubernetes

- 
You're interested in UX, UI design, and the research field

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture. 

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package. 

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

- 
Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

- 
Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

- 
Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Benefits

- 
Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid

- 
For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our benefits pages for more information

- 
Free access to proper mental health care, unlimited virtual therapy sessions (with a human) and 24/7 access to resources

- 
Life and Disability Insurance, 100% of the team member premium paid

- 
Flexible time off

- 
Meaningful equity

- 
Company retreats, fully paid for by Maze

- 
New MacBook (laptop), paid for by Maze

- 
Paid Family leave: 16 weeks for birth or adoptive parents

- 
$500/month to be used for dependent health insurance coverage 

- 
If you don't have dependents to add to your plan, you will still get access to this money to be used at your discretion to get the benefits that matter to you with our flexible a-maze-ing benefits - gym memberships, co-working spaces, food, travel, whatever!

- 
$1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space

- 
Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours

- 
Monthly Bonus.ly points that are awarded to others to recognize teamwork, dedication and helpfulness - points can be cashed out for gift cards and more

- 
Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year 

- 
SWAG, we have some really cool swag

- 
Open, transparent culture that includes virtual: coffee chats, bi-weekly all-hands meetings, and more

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits here . 

Outreach Notice

We understand you might be excited about the job you’re applying for, we are excited you are interested! However, please refrain from reaching out to our current team members on LinkedIn for referrals. Our policy is that referrals can only be provided by team members who personally know the candidate. With the high volume of interest in our roles, contacting our team members who are not involved in recruitment can be overwhelming. title: Backend Engineer (Node.js / TypeScript)
description:
About Nexoya

We help marketing teams unlock their growth potential with AI. Our attribution shows how advertising investments perform across channels, and our optimizations shift budgets to where they drive the bottom line. Leading European brands in e-commerce, telco, banking, insurance, energy and more rely on us.

The role

You build and run the Node.js/TypeScript services behind the Nexoya app: the GraphQL API, ad channel integrations and data ingestion, and new LLM- and agent-based features. You join a team of about 10 engineers across backend, ML, frontend and platform, and you own your features from design to production.

How we build software

AI coding agents change how software gets built, but not who is responsible for it.

- Decisions are made together. Important technical decisions start as an Architecture Decision Record reviewed by the team. Good arguments win, not seniority.

- Engineers design, agents implement. Your design is the input for our coding agents, guided by a shared rule set in our agent harness that the team evolves together.

- Working is not done. Code is ready when it is maintainable: readable, tested, robust on unhappy paths. Larger changes are reviewed, so at least two engineers know every change.

- You build it, you run it. A rotating internal support duty shows us which decisions worked.

What you will do

- Ship backend features end to end on our Kubernetes-based Azure cloud.

- Evolve our GraphQL API with clear schemas and stable contracts.

- Build reliable ad channel integrations and data ingestion with MySQL and RabbitMQ.

- Build AI features such as our in-app assistant (tool calling, retrieval, structured outputs), with evaluation, monitoring and guardrails.

- Help evolve our agent harness and raise the bar for tests, reviews and documentation.

What you bring

- [3+] years as a Backend Engineer with Node.js and TypeScript.

- Solid API design (GraphQL or REST) and MySQL experience.

- Experience with message brokers and running services on Docker, Kubernetes and a major cloud (Azure preferred).

- You enjoy discussing design trade-offs in writing and care about code others can maintain.

- Fluent English.

Bonus: ad platform APIs (Google Ads, Meta) or attribution; AI or agent features in production (Anthropic/OpenAI APIs, MCP, RAG); LLM evaluation or observability; team use of Claude Code or similar; data pipelines; German.

What we offer

- Direct impact on how enterprise marketers allocate their budgets.

- Real ownership in a team that takes engineering quality seriously.

- A genuine AI-first culture: experiment, automate, share.

- A transparent culture at eye level, with regular team events.

- Strategy Days twice a year where the whole team shapes company strategy (past: Helsinki, Berlin, Belgrade, Swiss Alps, Zurich).

Application process

- Profile review and phone screen

- Take-home assignment: a backend feature

- Technical discussion with the engineering team

- [On-site] interview and team evaluation

title: Senior software engineer (Node.js/TypeScript)
description:
Hybrid working based at one of our offices in London, Bath or Edinburgh. Your contract will be hybrid, although we don’t currently require a set number of office days. We support flexible working and trust teams to agree how and where they work best, taking a pragmatic approach based on the needs of the role and team. 

About us 

Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.

We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.

We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.

We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.

If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.

Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.

Our culture: 

Never settle – We think of ourselves as ‘embedded hero-makers’ for our customers. We put them first, and if we say we’ll do something, we’ll move heaven and earth to do it. We think boldly and embrace change.

Take ownership - We think rigorously and deeply about a problem, but then charge at it, acting with and urgency and speed that sets us apart. But we never lose sight of quality or long-term scalability.

Be generous & candid - We encourage our people – and our customers – to challenge us and never shy away from tough conversations. We have a flat and inclusive culture where everyone can be themselves – and speak up.

Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team. 

Our engineering ways of working: 

- Our Product and Engineering organisation is structured into four tribes: Custody, Accounts, Experience, and Cloud & Security. Each tribe contains multiple autonomous squads, with clear full ownership over specific product domains.

- The squads are intentionally small and cross-functional, typically made up of an Engineering Manager, Product Manager, and 3–5 engineers with complementary skills aligned to the domain they own.

- We operate in a build-and-run model, with teams responsible for the full software lifecycle, from architecture and delivery through to operational support and incident management.

- Our core platform is built on AWS serverless technologies including Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway, S3, and ECS. We primarily develop in TypeScript and Node.js, with MongoDB as our primary document database. We also have a small number of C# services and are continuing to evolve our platform architecture, including expanding our use of ECS Fargate.

- Infrastructure is managed through a combination of Terraform and Serverless Framework. We use GitHub Actions for CI/CD and incident.io to support our incident management processes and operational workflows.

- We care deeply about engineering quality, pragmatic architecture, and continuous improvement. If you’d like to go deeper, we’re happy to share more about our engineering practices and technology radar during the interview process.

The role 

As an engineer at Seccl you will design, build and operate reliable and scalable, testable and maintainable software solutions, building new functionalities and products using Typescript and Node.js. You play a key role in our software development and have a hands-on approach throughout the development process supporting resilient financial workflow systems and regulated investment operations. As a senior member of the team, you are the ‘go-to’ person for queries. 

On a typical day you will… 

- Work collaboratively in a domain aligned cross-functional squad made up of engineers and product along with colleagues from customer-facing and operations teams

- Design, implement and operate your services within your domain

- Be accountable for the SLAs of your products and iterative improvements

- Maintain and extend documentation for your services

- Foster a culture of continuous improvement and technical excellence while understanding when “good enough for now” is appropriate

- Provide guidance and mentorship for other engineers

- Communicate with non-technical colleagues to answer queries about the Seccl system

What you need… 

- To own your services from design to operation. We operate a build-and-run model where engineers have autonomy but full accountability.

- We care deeply about correctness, resilience and operational excellence because our systems underpin real customer investments.

- Engineers are not passengers in their products but champions. Drive improvements and features while collaborating openly with product, operations and engineering colleagues, challenging ideas constructively and focusing on delivering the best outcomes for customers.

- Have a strong ability to understand business and customer problems and turn them into efficient, scalable solutions. Be curious about how investment and custody products operate, and pragmatic in balancing customer value, operational correctness, engineering quality and long-term scalability.

- Experience building financial systems with multi-region, multi-currency or trading-related complexity would be advantageous.

- Experience in a strongly/statically typed language.

- Have a strong understanding of designing, building, and running high-quality, standards-compliant workflow APIs, with a focus on testing, observability, and performance.

- Have worked with a cloud provider (AWS/Azure/GCP). We use AWS.

- Have worked with distributed systems and are comfortable debugging through tracing and observability.

- Willing to be on-call for your services.

Core technical skills you must have: 

- Strong commercial experience with Node.js , specifically TypeScript 

- Experience with Amazon Web Services 

- Experience with Serverless products

- Experience with document databases, ideally MongoDB 

- Experience mentoring engineers

- Experience leading technical delivery in a build-and-run engineering model

- Experience in a structured on-call process and incident management

- Experience working in regulated industries, ideally financial services or FinTech.

This role isn’t for you if... 

- You rely on a lot of top-down direction. Here, you’ll have a lot of freedom and ownership of your role, and you’ll be expected to shape your own progression, bring forward ideas, and spot opportunities to improve

- You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet

- You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen

- You don’t like change . You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty

What’s in it for you… 

We offer a generous mix of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including:

Base salary based on experience and skills demonstrated during our assessment phase

🌴 27 days holiday + bank holidays (some can be flexible) + day off on your birthday + three days (full time) per year for Dependant leave

💙 Two volunteering days per year 

🏅 Length of service award – one month paid sabbatical at eight years

✅ 6% employer pension contribution, and life assurance

🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health

👪 Enhanced Parental leave

💻 MacBook and up to £500 home office set up budget

📖 £750 per person learning budget

🌎 Option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year

🌻 Health and wellbeing initiatives including free therapy via Wellness Cloud, mental health support via Headspace

🌱 Strong financial wellbeing focus including access to Octopus Money , Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing offering via Octopus Legacy 

🎁 Perkbox – Flexi-points giving you a range of discounts and perks including free weekly coffee, gym and retail discounts

🚲 Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing

Interview process 

Interviewing is a two-way thing, and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you. Our interviews are conversational, so come with questions and be curious. In general, you can expect the interview process to look a bit like this:

- Talent screen - 30 min intro call with our Talent partner or an Engineering manager

- Bar raiser - 40 min with two Engineering leaders focused on Engineering culture alignment

- Technical loop - 2h virtual technical assessment with 2 core components - system design, TypeScript code review with breaks between the stages. You will receive preparation materials for the round and more information on how to prepare.

⏳ We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out and you should expect to hear back from us within one to two weeks of applying.

🌈 Our aim is to build a diverse and inclusive company of awesome people, with unique skills, passions and experiences. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you!

title: Senior Fullstack Software Engineer
description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

The Work 

Fullstack at Headway means end-to-end ownership. You’re building reliable abstraction layers over a fragmented healthcare system and translating them into seamless, empathetic user experiences. What you could work on:

- 
The Modern AI-enabled Clinical System: Help design and build the interfaces and systems that manage clinical data. Build high-integrity experiences for treatment plans and progress notes, integrating AI-powered clinical intelligence to give providers their time back.

- 
Therapist Practice Management: Build a best-in-class platform for Headway therapists to run their businesses. You'll own features from the database schema to the UI, creating intuitive web experiences for scheduling, clinical notes, and payment management.

- 
Patient-First Experiences: We’re moving toward a patient-centric model. Transform the therapist search experience by building the frontend interfaces and backend APIs that power personalized care recommendations, longitudinal data views, and seamless patient-provider matching.

- 
Frictionless Onboarding: Turn the historically nightmare process of insurance credentialing into a sleek, consumer-grade web experience. Build products and tooling to get providers in-network and scaling their practice in record time.

Our Stack 

- 
Languages: TypeScript, Python 3

- 
Frontend: React, Remix, Next.js

- 
Backend & Storage: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Postgres, Redis, Snowflake

- 
Infrastructure: AWS, Temporal, Kafka

- 
Ops: Datadog, Sentry, PagerDuty

- 
AI Tools: Cursor, Claude, Gemini, Eddy (our in-house cloud agent harness)

Who You Are 

- 
End-to-End Product Builder: You care just as much about the API architecture as you do the user experience. You seamlessly context-switch between backend logic and frontend state management.

- 
AI Frontier Tinkerer: You don't just use AI tools - you push their limits. You've experimented with applying LLMs to real workflows, whether that's code generation, operational automation, or developer tooling. You bring a builder's mindset: what can we automate, what should stay human, and how do we ship it responsibly in healthcare?

- 
Owns Outcomes, Not Tasks: You've been handed ambiguous problems and turned them into shipped software. You know how to define the solution, pull in the right people across teams, and keep things moving when priorities shift.

- 
Sets the Technical Standard: You make technical decisions that optimize for maintainability and scale, not just shipping speed. You proactively improve your team's engineering velocity - whether that's refining tooling, improving automation, or establishing patterns that prevent entire categories of bugs.

- 
Mentor by Default: You pull engineers into design discussions without being asked. Your code reviews teach, not just gatekeep. You make sure knowledge gets shared across the team, not siloed in one person's head.

- 
Ships Fast, Iterates Faster: You can move from problem statement to working solution quickly. You'd rather ship a good v1 this week than a perfect v1 next month. Real feedback from therapists and patients is worth more than another round of design review.

- 
Quick Study in Complex Domains: Healthcare is a maze of payers, regulations, and exceptions. You don't need prior healthcare experience, but you need to be someone who dives into unfamiliar domains and builds a working mental model fast.

- 
Motivated by Impact: You want your engineering skills applied to problems that matter. Mental healthcare access is broken in America, and you want to be part of fixing it.

- 
Communicates with Precision: Whether it's a Slack thread, a design doc, or a cross-team meeting, you communicate clearly and concisely. You know that great engineering is wasted if you can't bring people along.

Our Interview Process 

After you apply to Headway, here are some details of what to expect during the interview process.

- 
Initial screen : You’ll connect with someone in recruiting so you can learn more about the team, Headway’s mission and exciting growth, and we can get a better idea of your background. 

- 
First round: You'll do a live coding interview with Karat, our technical interviewing partner. It's a great opportunity to showcase your problem-solving skills and learn more about what our engineering team is building.

- 
Final rounds : You’ll meet several team members for technical and non-technical interviews and leave with a fuller picture of what it’s like to work at Headway.

- 
References and the Offer : Our favorite part of the process! We'll send over all of the details, including specifics on employee equity, and congratulatory messages from excited future team members!

Compensation & Benefits 

- 
Salary: $182,750 - $278,500 base salary plus a competitive equity package.

- 
Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k), Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and 16-week parental leave.

- 
The Mission: We reimburse your therapy and provide a professional development budget. We believe in what we’re building.

- 
Time Off: 13 holidays, a full week off in December, and flexible PTO.

We believe a team's strength is in its people, and we cannot achieve this mission without a team that reflects the diversity of this problem – across race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, age, national origin, religion, family status, disability, military status, and experience. title: Senior Fullstack Engineer
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

The team

At blp, dedicated engineering teams own individual products such as invoices, customer orders, and order confirmations. The Platform Team owns what all of them are built on: shared services and APIs, the data access layer, and the component and design system that shape how the product looks and behaves.

The team's focus has been the frontend platform, and we are now deliberately extending that ownership deeper into the stack. You would be central to that shift, with real influence over how the platform layer gets defined rather than inheriting someone else's blueprint.

About the role

- What you'll do and for whom. You build and run the core backend service our product teams rely on, from its APIs and persistence layer to email, user provisioning, and cross-tenant capabilities for large enterprises. Through those teams, your work reaches the 20'000+ people who use our Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash agents every day.

- Where you'll work. You join the Platform Team, about 10 engineers. At BLP, platform means the core of our product, not internal infrastructure: the shared services, data access layer, and design system that every product runs on. You work closely with the senior backend engineer who owns these areas today, in a large production Go codebase with well-established patterns.

- What success looks like. In your first year, you own one core area end-to-end, for example, user provisioning, outbound email, cross-tenant capabilities, analytics, or workflow configuration, from the Go service to the customer using it.

What you'll do

- Build the service that product teams build on. Design, build, and evolve the core APIs behind document processing, approval workflows, administration, and analytics, with clear contracts so product teams can ship on top of them without workarounds.

- Own the persistence layer. Each tenant has its own isolated MySQL database. You evolve the abstraction product teams build on (a tenant-scoped unit of work, typed repositories, and shared type-safe querying) so that isolation, transactions, and permissions are right by default.

- Scale BLP for large enterprises. Extend our cross-tenant capabilities so customers with many subsidiaries and business units can manage users, permissions, and documents across all of them from one place, correctly, securely, and fast.

- Own email, in and out. Own our email document ingestion and outbound email services, including the audit trail and its UI.

- Make setup self-service. Turn manual SSO, SCIM, and email setups into migration tools and admin UIs that customers and project managers can run on their own.

- Work with customers. Join onboarding calls with customer IT teams and project managers, get their setups running, and turn what you learn into better tooling.

- Own it end-to-end. From the Go service through the React UI to production, including tracing, metrics, and incident analysis after it ships.

Tech stack: Go, React/TypeScript, MySQL, Redis, Temporal, Kubernetes on GCP and AWS, GitHub CI/CD, and OpenTelemetry with Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, and Parca for observability.

We're excited about you because 

- You have 4+ years of experience as a software engineer , with most of that time spent building and operating backend systems in production.

- You have 2+ years of professional Go experience , writing services that run in production, not side projects.

- You've designed a backend service or API that other teams depended on, and kept it reliable and evolvable as usage grew.

- You work well across teams. You align with product, integration, and infrastructure teams on contracts, priorities, and rollouts, and you can explain technical trade-offs to people who aren't engineers.

- You improve existing production systems step by step, and you know when a rewrite isn't worth it.

- You have strong fundamentals in type systems, composition, testing, and clean architecture, and you're comfortable working in a codebase built on functional patterns.

- You're fullstack where it counts: you build on the components and design system our frontend experts maintain to ship admin UIs quickly, even though the backend is where you do your deepest work.

- You think in products and take ownership. You translate business problems into precise specifications, weigh cost against benefit, work directly with customers when a setup needs it, and stay responsible for what you ship after it goes live.

Strong plus 

- Experience with distributed systems , Kubernetes, Temporal, or cloud infrastructure.

- Experience with user provisioning (SCIM) and SSO (OIDC).

- Experience running multi-tenant systems.

- Domain knowledge in ERP, finance, procurement, or supply chain processes, or German language skills.

What you'll get 

- Ownership of visible outcomes. The areas you own decide how fast enterprise customers go live and how well BLP scales with them.

- Impact at scale. Every improvement you ship to the product core multiplies across all product teams and the 20'000+ people who use BLP daily.

- Senior scope from day one. You'll lead technical initiatives and mentor engineers on a team that is actively growing its backend ownership.

Learn more about BLP and our values at blp.digital/company/careers .

Please note: Hybrid work in London office, or remote in wider UK and Europe.

title: Lead Software Engineer
description:

Are you a driven person who wants to make buildings come alive?

We are Zurich Soft Robotics (ZSR), a Zurich-based startup developing Solskin – a climate-adaptive solar facade. Solskin is not just a PV system or a shading system; it’s an intelligent skin that uses weather and building data, occupant feedback, and AI algorithms to decide how the facade moves, so buildings stay comfortable, avoid overheating, and use energy as efficiently as possible. Solskin is already running on several buildings across Switzerland, with many more to follow.

In this role, you own the software that makes that happen. You write the code that runs Solskin, keep it reliable in the field, and constantly improve it. You will also architect and lead our future sensor-to-data platform. Your focus is where software meets hardware, and the control and AI on top of it. You don't need to be a front-end specialist.

What you will do

This is a hands-on leadership position: you code every day.

Own the full stack: You maintain and develop the whole software stack, from cloud and data management to user-facing applications, and from low-level embedded firmware to high-level AI controllers learning from users. You keep it reliable and keep making it better.

Be the link between the teams: You build the software that runs on real buildings and support the hardware team. You also build the internal tools used by sales and the business team. 

Lead what comes next : With the CEO and CTO, you set the software direction and lead development of future products. 

Our stack: 

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch

- Frontend: React, TypeScript

- Hardware: C/C++, STM32 microcontrollers, Beckhoff PLCs

- Database: PostgreSQL (TimescaleDB)

- DevOps & Cloud: Linux, Docker, AWS, Grafana

What we are looking for

Required: 

- Education : MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or similar.

- Python : This is a must. You write clean Python that runs in production, on real systems.

- Embedded & Hardware: Shipped C/C++ on microcontrollers running on physical hardware; comfortable working with sensors, actuators, and basic electronics. 

- Applied AI & Control: Understanding of modern control and ML/RL methods, with hands-on PyTorch experience applied to physical or dynamic systems.

- Cloud & data : You are comfortable with PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS.

- Leadership attitude : You take ownership, make decisions, and want to grow as a leader.

- Languages : English. German is a big plus.

- Hybrid setting : You will be expected to be on-site at least three days per week, and sometimes at customers’ locations, to work on real products.

- Availability : 100%, as soon as possible.

- Work-permit: You need the right to work in Switzerland for this position.

Preferred: 

- Startup experience: You have worked in a startup before and know what that means.

- Building modeling and control: You have prior experience handling building data, modeling building dynamics, and developing building controllers; ideally with ML and RL tools. 

- Frontend: React and TypeScript.

Mindset: 

- Hands-on: You lead, and you still do the hard work yourself.

- Fast: You are pragmatic and iterate quickly. Things break, and plans change, and that doesn't scare you.

- Purpose: You care about climate and want to make buildings smarter.

Benefits

Impact: Your code runs on real buildings. You see the result of your work.

Ownership: A key role with a real say in our product and technology, and room to grow with the company.

Flexibility: Hybrid work and flexible hours. We like being in the Zurich office together, so plan for regular office days.

Team: A small, skilled, and down-to-earth team that helps each other out.

The reality: We are a startup. It is often messy; things rarely work the first time, and the workload is real. In return, you get a lot of freedom and responsibility from day one.

Sounds like you?

Send us your CV and a short document instead of a classic cover letter. It doesn’t need to be long, just enough for us to understand who you are and where you stand. Please cover these points:

- About you: A short description of yourself.

- Proud of: One thing you are really proud of, in a few sentences.

- Startup: Why do you fit a startup?

- Software meets hardware: Your experience where software and hardware come together.

- Juggeling many hats: You’ll rarely finish one thing from A to Z without interruptions: different stacks, different people, different projects, and on-site surprises. Describe a time your work was like that, and how you handled it.

title: Head of Technology
description:
We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link 

About garden3d 

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

Weâre the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development 

At Sanctuary Computer weâre building a different type of technology shop â one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design 

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and weâve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

Weâre building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community 

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK â Media 

At garden3d, weâre in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone 
Mill 
IngredientAI 

â°ï¸ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates 

ï¸ Systems that hold up 

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development 

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering 

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer 

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best 

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery 

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business 

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense 

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story 

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture 

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Â Special Projects 

In addition to day to day responsibilities, hereâs an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years â

- Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts
- Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from
- Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do
- Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio
- Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products
- Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed
Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have: 

- 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company
- Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products
- A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native
- A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure
- All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase
- Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it
- Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients
- A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them
- Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)
Nice-to-have: 

- A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products
- Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)
- Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role
- Open source projects they've started or maintained
- Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams
- Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company
- A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring
- Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality
Who you are

The person weâre looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. Theyâre flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work âsmartâ by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, weâll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where weâre going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

title: Principal Forward Deployed Engineer (EMEA)
description:
About Docker 

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

The Role 

Docker Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) embed directly with our most strategic customers to solve important, complex technical problems and turn ambitious ideas into production outcomes. FDEs take on the most challenging technical challenges using existing Docker products and patterns when possible, and work across customer, Docker Product and Engineering teams to realize new approaches when required.

As a Docker FDE, you will work side-by-side with customer engineering teams to deeply understand their goals, problems, constraints, and technical landscape; identify the highest-leverage opportunities; and design, build, and ship solutions with them. You own the technical journey from discovery and architecture through prototyping, implementation and production rollout.

The solutions you build may use existing Docker products, extend Docker into new environments, integrate deeply with customer and third-party systems, or reveal capabilities that Docker should build next. You work closely with Docker Solutions Architects to evolve existing patterns, and Docker Product and Engineering to turn new learnings into reusable patterns and product capabilities.

_______________________________________________________________________

Responsibilities 

Build in Production with Customers 

- Embed with customer engineering teams to design, build, and ship solutions from first prototype through stable production rollout. Use existing Docker products and patterns when possible, invent, prototype and validate innovative solutions when necessary.

- Deliver working technical artifacts to customers: custom MCP servers with tightly integrated Docker Sandbox environments for coding agents and containerized agents; Docker Compose definitions for multi-agent harnesses and model-backed applications; Hardened Image standardization and migration; New tools that unblock customer progress.

- Integrate Docker's AI platform with the customer's existing stack, including identity providers (OIDC/SAML/SSO), secrets management, private and air-gapped registries, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tooling.

- Own technical delivery on your engagements: scope the work, sequence it, make trade-offs between speed and quality, remove blockers early, and contribute directly to code whenever progress depends on it.

Make AI Adoption Safe and Governable 

- Translate customer security, compliance, and platform requirements into concrete plans and see those plans through from ideation to production.

- Help customers define controls to enable them to adopt agentic AI to solve their unique business problems without compromising security, compliance, data sovereignty or end-user experience.

- Establish quality and performance standards for customers and work closely with Docker Product and Engineering to quickly address issues that fall outside of established thresholds

- Partner with customer security and platform teams to get agentic workloads through architecture review, threat modeling, and change control.

Partner with Solutions Architecture and the Field 

- Work closely with Solutions Architects to enable off-the-self solutions when possible and provide technical experience and leadership when a bespoke solution is necessary.

- Feed implementation learnings back into reference architectures, SOW templates, and success patterns so that FDE innovations become standard features and implementation patterns.

- Support the field with technical depth during proofs of concept, escalations, and expansion conversations when a working build is the fastest path to a customer adoption.

Close the Loop with Product and Engineering 

- As part of Docker Engineering FDEs work closely with Product and Engineering teams to fold FDE innovations, learnings, and design patterns into existing or new products and services.

- Work with Customers, Product and Engineering to establish quality and performance thresholds, ensuring customer environments meet them consistently, and responding quickly and decisively when they don’t.

- Be the voice of the customer. Deliver data-driven and actionable feedback to Product and Engineering: what works well; what does not; what customers are asking for; and what blocks their adoption and forward progress. FDE experience directly influences the roadmap.

Shape the Practice 

- Define the FDE engagement model, delivery standards, and quality bar, and codify them so that engagements are consistent across customers, regions, and delivery partners.

- Mentor and lead other Forward Deployed Engineers, and participate in hiring loops to grow the team.

- Act as the senior technical escalation point on the hardest problems impacting your customers. Every incident is an opportunity to improve Docker products and services.

- Maintain deep, current knowledge of the agentic AI stack: LLMs, APIs, MCP, coding agents, model and harness evaluation approaches, performance and quality thresholds, deployment patterns.

- This role may require participation in an on-call rotation to provide support outside of standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

_______________________________________________________________________

Qualifications 

Required 

- 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Professional Services Engineer, or Software Engineer with consulting or technical founder experience.

- Technical leadership across multiple engagements, teams, or domains, with a proven ability to set delivery standards, define repeatable patterns, and influence product direction through field evidence.

- Expert production coding skills in Go, Python, or TypeScript, with a track record of shipping and operating software that other people depend on and of leading technical design reviews.

- Deep, hands-on Docker expertise: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, Docker Compose, image and registry operations, container networking and storage, and container security fundamentals.

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents in production, including tool use and function calling, the Model Context Protocol (MCP server and client implementation), prompt and context engineering, and evaluation of agent behavior.

- Working knowledge of software supply chain security: SBOMs, image signing and attestation, vulnerability management, minimal and hardened base images, and secure CI/CD.

- Experience integrating with enterprise systems: identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, LDAP/Active Directory), federated identity protocols (OIDC, SAML), secrets managers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP).

- Ability to scope and deliver complex work in ambiguous, fast-moving customer environments, making sound trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality.

- Excellent communication skills with engineers, security and platform teams, and executive stakeholders, with a low-ego, collaborative approach and the ability to lead through influence rather than authority.

- Proven track record of technical mentorship and of raising the bar for the engineers around you.

- High agency and comfort operating autonomously in distributed, remote-first teams.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Travel to customer sites to build in person with customer teams, estimated at up to 50%.

Bonus 

- Experience with Docker Hardened Images, Docker Scout, MCP Gateway, MCP Toolkit, Docker Sandboxes, or Docker Model Runner.

- Experience deploying and operating coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or similar) in team or enterprise settings.

- Experience with air-gapped, regulated, or compliance-driven environments in financial services, healthcare, government, or similar sectors.

- Contributions to open source projects in the container, Kubernetes, or MCP ecosystems.

- Prior experience founding or scaling a Forward Deployed Engineering or Professional Services practice.

Visa sponsorship: Docker considers visa sponsorship on a case-by-case basis based on business needs.

_______________________________________________________________________

Compensation & Equity 

All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

Europe: €121K – €198K base

______________________________________________________________________

Posting Information 

- Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

- AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

- Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________

Perks & Benefits 

- Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

- Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

- Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

- Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

- Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

- Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

- Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

- Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

- Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

- Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community.

title: Full-Stack Engineer - Broker Terms Team
description:
Full-Stack Engineer - Broker Terms Team

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Full-Stack Engineer to join the Broker Terms team. 

You’ll build the systems behind every offer iwoca makes through brokers, and see your work in the terms each business gets.

The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

Broker Terms is a growing team that owns the full offer terms strategy for businesses that come to iwoca through a broker – both first-time and repeat customers. It sets pricing, loan amounts, durations, and broker commissions, and owns the offer user interface (UI) brokers use in the Introducer Portal. The broker network is iwoca's biggest acquisition channel, and the team is directly responsible for the terms that win those customers.

The team is small and interdisciplinary – commercial strategy, engineering and data science. It turns business questions into quantitative problems, and findings into timely decisions. It works on short-term gains and longer-term bets, and judges both by Customer Lifetime Value – what a business is worth to iwoca across all its borrowing.

There are no fixed office days, and the team meets up for lunch once or twice a month.

The role 

As a full-stack engineer in Broker Terms, you'll make changes across iwoca's codebase wherever they'd improve an offer. Most of it is backend – the code that calculates each offer's terms – with some frontend on the UI where brokers see them.

You'll own features and projects from scoping and design through to production, and choose how to build them. You'll help decide what goes on the team's roadmap. You'll learn from the team's experienced engineers, and from the people who price broker offers.

The team is light on process – a daily stand-up, a weekly meeting and regular retrospectives – and you'll have a say in how it works. Brokers see your changes in the Introducer Portal, and A/B tests show you which ones raised Customer Lifetime Value. Your work helps businesses get the funding they need.

Live project examples:

- Model-based pricing. Developing the systems that let a model set bespoke pricing for each customer.

- No-fee test. Testing how the product performs without drawdown fees, and how that changes the way customers repay.

- Loan durations. Building longer-duration Flexi-Loans with flexible repayments.

- Offer display. Improving how offers appear to brokers and customers – a better journey, and easier testing for the team's data scientists.

- Commission systems. Upgrading iwoca's broker commission systems.

The requirements 

Essential:

- Backend engineering. You've designed and built backend systems that run in production, ideally in Python, Django and PostgreSQL. You've modelled their data with performance and maintenance in mind.

- Frontend engineering. You've built and maintained user interfaces in production, ideally in TypeScript and React.

- Ownership. You've taken features end to end, and kept them working once people relied on them.

- Trade-offs. You've weighed delivery speed against the long-term health of a system, and can explain what you chose and why.

- AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

- DevOps. You've used containers and CI/CD pipelines to deploy your code.

- Experimentation. You've worked on A/B tests or other experiments, and used the results to decide what to build next.

- Product thinking. You've found the business need behind a feature request, and planned the technical work to meet it.

- Financial services. You've worked on lending, payments or pricing systems.

The salary 

We expect to pay from £60,000 to £85,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture 

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

You'll work at the intersection of three things: shipping features end-to-end in Priva Digital Services (touching both backend and, where needed, the front end), integrating optimization and forecasting logic into production services , and strengthening the cloud/DevOps foundation the whole department builds on. Our Digital Twin and optimization technologies exist to meet that shift at scale, delivering measurable results such as lower energy intensity, greater flexibility and reliability, reduced operating costs, and structurally lower emissions. 

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you'll help turn that ambition into production reality: building the services, integrations, and cloud foundation that put our optimization and forecasting capabilities to work for customers every day. 

Your work will directly contribute to:

What You’ll Do

Optimization & forecasting integration

Cloud infrastructure & DevOps 

- Own and improve cloud infrastructure (Azure) that supports scalability across Energy Solutions teams

What you will NOT do 

- This is not a research or modelling role. You implement and integrate optimization and forecasting models rather than developing new theory 

- You are not expected to be a dedicated front-end specialist or a dedicated DevOps specialist. The role spans these areas by design, so depth in every direction isn't the bar 

- A bachelor's degree in an IT-related field 

- Around 5 years of experience in a software engineering role, with demonstrated range across at least two of the following: backend/production systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end, or optimization integration. Versatility across these areas matters more here than deep tenure in a single one

- Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to work with complex, unfamiliar systems 

- A passion for creating customer value through high-quality engineering 

- Curiosity, ownership, craftsmanship, and the drive to keep learning 

- Good communication skills, able to explain trade-offs clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders 

- A good vibe: you bring energy to the team and make collaboration genuinely enjoyable, not just effective 

What We Offer You

🌴 30 days holiday per year, with the option to buy 5 extra at half price

🎉 A vibrant, open culture where you can be yourself

🍻 Twice-weekly drinks on Thursdays and Fridays

title: AI Native Product Engineer
description:
At Brevo, we’re not just building a CRM. With our technology, we’re helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. 

From emails and SMS to WhatsApp, Chat, and Marketing Automation, our tools are intuitive, powerful, and built to scale with every ambition. We give businesses a clear view of the customer journey, so they can focus on what matters: connection.

As a certified B Corp , we’re proud to grow with purpose, committed to high standards of social and environmental impact, not just performance.

Today, more than 500,000 businesses across 180 countries —from NGOs like Amnesty International to global brands like Carrefour, eBay, Louis Vuitton, and Michelin—trust Brevo to engage their audiences, cut through complexity, and deliver results. Our reliable technology and 75+ integrations help them create unparalleled customer experiences, without the usual tech headaches.

We recently exceeded 200m ARR and reached a major milestone by becoming a Unicorn , backed by strong growth and global expansion - and we’re just getting started!

The role: 

Join us as a Product Engineer to build a new product within Brevo called Brevo OS.

Brevo OS is a startup inside Brevo: a team of six, a product we started from an empty repository earlier this year, and the feel of a small company within the big one. The product works, the first customer deployments are beginning, and a great deal is still undecided — so the people who join us now will shape what it becomes.
It's an AI-native operating system for small businesses: a system of agents that helps a solopreneur, a hair salon or a building contractor run their whole business — clients, contracts and signature, invoicing, their website, their inbox. Modules get added the way an ERP grows, except the whole thing is built around agents from the ground up.

Your Impact at Brevo: 

- Turn a very high level business need into something real : understand the function, define the users, the smallest useful version, the entities and their lifecycles, the permissions and constraints that matter, and what to build versus integrate

- Decide which of our platform primitives to extend rather than reinvent, then build it, ship it, watch it in production, and improve it

- Work across product management, frontend, backend, data modelling, infrastructure, and AI. Everyone arrived with a specialism and nobody is confined to theirs; product thinking and business analysis is part of everyone’s job

- Build almost entirely through coding agents: Claude Code is the workflow, not a pilot running alongside it, for implementation, codebase exploration, documentation, debugging, and operations

- Decompose problems into work an agent can actually execute, give it context without over-constraining it, and tell the difference between correct and merely plausible

- Verify with tests and instrumentation, not vibes, and keep a large generated codebase coherent

- Work day to day in TypeScript, Kubernetes, and agentic frameworks

Who you are: 

- Around 2-5 years of professional engineering experience. We care more about your slope than your years.

- Real depth in something, and no attachment to staying there. Bring what you're genuinely strong at — the team compounds those — and expect to spend a good part of your time well outside it.

- Coding agents already central to how you work. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, something equivalent. Not "I've generated the Unit Tests" — real delegation of substantial work, and real review of what comes back. Scepticism about generated output is a feature of this job, not a problem.

- Evidence you've owned a problem, not just implemented a ticket — something you helped define, drove, shipped and then lived with in production. Product questions are your questions too.

- At your best when the brief is one sentence and the plan is still moving . We're learning what this product is, so priorities change often. The mission doesn't.

- English. We're an international team working across France and India, and English is our working language. French is not required.

If you don't meet all the requirements above but believe this opportunity matches your expectations and experience, we still encourage you to apply!

Why people love working at Brevo: 

- A place to grow, together: Join an international team in a bright, collaborative office located in a vibrant neighbourhood.

- Practical perks for everyday balance: RTT days off, 50% public transport reimbursement, Sustainable Mobility Package (whether you ride a classic bike or go electric, we support your choice to commute greener) and daily Swile meal vouchers (€12.50/day).

- Learning, every step of the way: Access to English classes and 155,000+ courses on Udemy, plus a strong internal culture of knowledge-sharing and support.

- Flexible for life: A remote-friendly setup, budget to support your home workspace, and relocation assistance for international talents.

- Wellbeing that works: Top-notch private healthcare (70% covered), 6-week second-parent leave, extra time off if your child is sick and needs you, and several prevention, health and wellbeing services on the Welii platform.

- A culture that cares: From inter-office trips to regular team events, there are plenty of ways to connect beyond your day-to-day. You'll also find active social, green, and LGBTQIA+ communities, plus Work Council benefits via Leeto, all here to support what matters to you, inside and outside of work.

Our candidate journey: 

- Introductory TA call (30 min)

- Interview with our VP Engineering (60 min)

- Live Use case (2 hours)

- Final interview with the Global VP & People Business Partner (30 min)

Whoever you are, wherever you’re from, if this role speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you.

Nice to have: 

- Experience with PostGIS, GIS, mapping, or other geospatial systems

- Experience with LangGraph, LangChain, or multi-step ML and LLM workflows

- Experience deploying software on-prem, offline, or as an appliance

- Experience with front-end performance and data-dense interfaces

- Prior work in defence, government, or dual-use technology

What's In It For You

- Competitive package (top 0.1% of compensation in Europe: base + equity)

- Paris or London based

- End-to-end ownership of product used in real operational environments

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Mission 

Alan is scaling internationally (900+ employees, 100+ healthcare professionals, 5+ countries) and needs IT Operations Specialists to own device security, SaaS platforms, identity & access, and the daily IT experience of every Alaner, while contributing to build projects that remove operational toil.

First year

3 years

- Lead medium to high-complexity IT projects end-to-end

Must-have - Technical/hard skills:

Nice-to-have skills / Bonus points if you have:
