title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
About Juniper Square 

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

Our culture is built for people who want to do ambitious, meaningful work alongside exceptionally talented teammates. We think like owners, move with urgency, and take pride in solving hard problems that truly matter to our customers and the future of private markets. We believe the best ideas come from open debate, deep collaboration, and diverse perspectives, which is why we believe transparency is the default and feedback makes us stronger. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us!

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time. 

About your role 

As a Staff Software Engineer at Juniper Square, you are a technical leader - setting technical direction, driving architectural decisions, and raising engineering quality across your team. This is a player-coach role: you lead through code and architecture, not just direction. You'll write production code as a hands-on individual contributor while owning your team's technical strategy, roadmap, and growth, and you'll collaborate closely with product, design, and QA to turn complex workflows into delightful, intuitive experiences.

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer for the following team: 

- 
Treasury: Join the team building Juniper Square's Treasury platform, the system that brings transactions, balances, and bank data into and across the platform. You'll work on expanding bank integrations, a visualization and reporting layer for payments and treasury data, and vendor exports that connect treasury data to accounting, on a team that has already processed $500M+ in transactions.

What you'll do 

Own Technical Direction & Architecture 

- 
Set the technical direction and own the architecture for your domain's systems, from design through production

- 
Lead technical design for ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives - evaluating tradeoffs, aligning stakeholders, and driving implementation

- 
Be instrumental in your team's transition from monolith to service-oriented architecture

- 
Evaluate and select technologies with a bias toward what ships well and scales sustainably

Build & Deliver 

- 
Write production code as a hands-on individual contributor - this is not a role that delegates implementation to others

- 
Own end-to-end delivery of roadmap projects: design, coding, testing, and production

- 
Manage your team's short-term roadmap (spanning the next two quarters), proactively surfacing execution, cost, and technical risks and driving pragmatic mitigation

- 
Lead the development of complex, full-stack workflows, working across frontend and backend engineers

AI Fluency & AI-Native SDLC 

- 
Practice AI Fluency across the full software development lifecycle - deliberately choosing where AI versus traditional software is the right tool, and defending those tradeoffs against real criteria (latency, accuracy, cost, data sensitivity, explainability)

- 
Champion and embed AI-native development practices and tools (e.g., Cursor, Augment) to drive significant productivity gains across your team

- 
Adapt code review and testing practices for an AI-assisted SDLC - catching AI-specific failure modes (hallucinated dependencies, overconfident but incorrect logic) before they ship

- 
Build and evaluate agentic workflows and AI-assisted systems where they add real value, with clear human-in-the-loop boundaries and monitoring for failure

- 
Guard against over-reliance on AI tooling, in your own work and in the code you review, balancing velocity with system comprehension and accountability for outcomes

- 
Foster a culture of rapid iteration, high velocity, and quality, and help raise AI fluency across the team

Lead & Grow the Team 

- 
Mentor engineers, raise the quality of technical decision-making, and help the team execute with consistency

- 
Establish coding standards, review practices, and architectural documentation that scale as the team grows

- 
Partner with recruiting to build and grow the team

Collaborate Cross-Functionally 

- 
Work closely with product, design, QA, and customer support to translate requirements into executable technical plans

- 
Participate actively in design reviews and roadmap discussions with a grounded, implementation-level perspective

- 
Handle most cross-team conflicts and technical decisions autonomously

Operational Excellence 

- 
Own monitoring, diagnosing, and resolving production issues within your team's services

- 
Use observability tooling to measure and improve system performance and reliability

- 
Implement and uphold best practices that maximize developer productivity across the team

Domain Expertise 

- 
Grow into a subject-matter expert in your domain, with an in-depth understanding of customer needs and the value your systems deliver

Qualifications 

Required 

- 
12+ years of experience in backend and/or full-stack software engineering, with a clear trajectory of increasing technical leadership, architectural responsibility, and mentorship

- 
A portfolio of shipped production systems - be ready to walk through specific technical decisions you personally made and code you personally wrote; this is not a role for someone whose primary contribution has been directing others

- 
Deep expertise in at least one server-side language (Python preferred, Node/TS, Java, C++, C#, or similar) and strong proficiency building production-grade backend services

- 
Experience with modern front-end frameworks (React preferred) and comfort working full-stack when the problem calls for it

- 
Experience with relational/NoSQL databases, including schema design, performance tuning, and data modeling

- 
Experience building and operating cloud-native systems using AWS (or equivalent), Docker, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code

- 
Strong understanding of CI/CD, observability, reliability, and operational excellence in production environments

- 
Deep understanding of service-oriented architecture and experience evolving systems from monolith toward SOA

- 
Demonstrated ability to raise engineering quality through technical standards, design reviews, mentoring, and reusable platform patterns

- 
Hands-on experience with AI-native development tools (e.g., Cursor, Augment) and a track record of using them to accelerate personal and team velocity

- 
Demonstrated AI Fluency: hands-on experience building AI-assisted or agentic systems with a deliberate, defensible point of view on when AI is (and isn't) the right tool; adapted code review practices to catch AI-specific failure modes; and concrete safeguards against over-reliance on AI tooling

- 
Ability to work through ambiguity, break down complex problems, and drive alignment across engineering, product, and design

- 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent work experience

Nice to Have 

- 
Reporting: experience with data integration platforms, ETL/ELT processes, business intelligence tools, or financial data

- 
Production experience building AI/LLM-powered systems (RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks) 

- 
Background in financial document processing or fintech data pipelines

- 
Prior experience in a technical lead or TLM capacity on a new or early-stage product team

At Juniper Square, we believe building a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture makes us a better company. If you think this role sounds like a fit, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification.

Compensation 

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $190,000 – $235,000 USD and the Canadian base salary range is $180,000 - $225,000 CAD. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.

Benefits include:

• Health, dental, and vision care for you and your family

• Life insurance

• Mental wellness coverage

• Fertility and growing family support

• Flex Time Off in addition to company-paid holidays

• Paid family leave, medical leave, and bereavement leave policies

• Retirement saving plans

• Allowance to customize your work and technology setup at home

• Annual professional development stipend

Your recruiter can provide additional details about compensation and benefits.

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Mobility
description:
Join our expanding Mobility engineering team! We’re actively recruiting a Senior Backend Engineer as M-KOPA Mobility, our fast-growing e-mobility business, which has a 3x year-on-year growth rate! Build the event-driven microservices that power clean, affordable transport for riders and entrepreneurs across Africa, with AI tools like Claude Code alongside you. Because Mobility is scaling quickly, an entrepreneurial spirit will serve you well: you’ll enjoy building in a fast-growing business and taking real ownership.

The Impact – Africa’s transport sector is massive, underserved, and at an inflection point, and the shift to electric is accelerating, led by East Africa. Your code will directly power the technology behind Kenya’s leading e-mobility financing platform. M-KOPA has already served over 7 million customers and unlocked more than $2 billion in credit. In Mobility, we’ve financed over 11,000 electric motorbikes, helping riders save more than $3 a day and cutting air pollution by 90%. It’s your chance to build tech for a business that’s literally transforming lives across an entire continent 🌍

The Opportunity 

🚀 Scale challenges: M-KOPA Mobility is growing 3x year-on-year as its own fast-scaling business, with over 11,000 e-motorbikes financed and demand climbing. As it grows, so do the opportunities to expand your scope, your impact and your career

🎯 Mission-driven engineering: Every service you build helps put clean transport within reach of riders who’d otherwise be locked out of ownership

🏆 Global recognition: Join a company named by the Financial Times as one of Africa’s fastest-growing for 5 consecutive years (2022–2026)

🌱 Environmental impact: Electric is simply better for drivers, cities and the planet. Our e-motorbikes cut air pollution by 90% versus petrol equivalents

What You’ll Do 

At M-KOPA, you’ll build sophisticated event-driven microservices with real-world impact. Our engineering teams own their solutions end-to-end, from architecture decisions to production monitoring, using AI coding tools like Claude Code to move faster along the way. Join us in combining cutting-edge .NET development with purpose-driven engineering that makes digital and financial inclusion possible across Africa.

Technical Environment 💻 

- Languages & frameworks: C#/.NET

- Cloud: We work in Azure, and welcome experience across AWS or GCP

- Architecture: Event-driven systems and microservice development. We use Service Bus, and welcome experience with similar messaging technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ

title: Senior Software Engineer (Storage) - remote in the US
description:
Company Description

About Mirantis 

Mirantis is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications. By combining open source innovation with deep expertise in Kubernetes orchestration, Mirantis empowers platform engineering teams to deliver composable, production-ready developer platforms across any environment—on-premises, in the cloud, at the edge, or in sovereign data centers. As enterprises navigate the growing complexity of AI-driven workloads, Mirantis delivers the automation, GPU orchestration, and policy-driven control needed to manage infrastructure with confidence and agility. Committed to open standards and freedom from lock-in, Mirantis ensures that customers retain full control of their infrastructure strategy.

Job Description

Overview 

Design and build the software that provisions, integrates, and operates high-performance storage for GPU-accelerated compute and AI platforms. You will develop the control-plane services, drivers, and tooling that connect enterprise and scale-out storage systems to Kubernetes-based workloads across hybrid, edge, and air-gapped deployments built on the Mirantis K0rdent stack.

About the Role 

We are looking for a software engineer who thinks in systems and data paths — someone who can reason about throughput, latency, consistency, and failure across a storage stack, then express that understanding as clean, testable Go. The right candidate has built production software against real storage systems (whether enterprise NAS, scale-out, or object), understands what makes storage fast and reliable at scale, and prefers declarative automation over manual operations. You should be self-directed, comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end, and effective communicating technical decisions across teams.

Responsibilities 

1. Storage Software & Integration 

- Design and build control-plane services, drivers (e.g., CSI), and tooling that provision, configure, and operate storage for Kubernetes-based AI/compute workloads.

- Integrate high-performance storage platforms — Dell PowerScale, VAST, and comparable systems — into automated, declarative provisioning workflows.

- Build data-path, telemetry, and observability tooling to diagnose and resolve performance, reliability, and scaling issues.

2. Software & Automation 

- Write production-quality software — primarily in Go — with strong testing, code review, and operational rigor.

- Deliver infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu) and GitOps-driven pipelines (ArgoCD or Flux) for storage configuration and lifecycle.

- Support bare-metal and hybrid provisioning where storage intersects host and cluster bring-up.

3. Platform & Hybrid Delivery 

- Deliver storage integration for k0s-based Kubernetes via Cluster API (CAPI) and K0rdent management/child cluster topologies.

- Architect storage software for fully disconnected (air-gapped) environments, including local artifact/mirror connectivity (Harbor) and PKI/TLS considerations.

Qualifications

- 5+ years of software development, including production systems, with Go as a primary language.

- 5+ years building or integrating storage systems (distributed, scale-out, NAS, or object) at scale.

- Hands-on experience with high-performance storage platforms such as Dell PowerScale, VAST, or comparable technologies.

- Solid understanding of storage fundamentals: file/block/object models, throughput and latency behavior, caching, consistency, and failure modes.

- Experience with Kubernetes storage (CSI, persistent volumes, storage classes) and infrastructure-as-code.

- Strong written and verbal communication with technical audiences.

Preferred 

- Proficiency in Python and/or Rust in addition to Go.

- Experience with the Mirantis K0rdent stack (K0rdent Enterprise, K0rdent AI, k0s, MKE) and Cluster API.

- Experience developing storage for GPU/AI workloads (high-throughput data pipelines, GPUDirect Storage).

- Proven experience in sovereign or high-security air-gapped environments.

Additional Information

What does Mirantis offer you? 
- Work with an established Silicon Valley leader in the cloud infrastructure industry;

- Work with exceptionally passionate, talented and engaging colleagues, helping Fortune 500 and Global 2000 customers implement next-generation cloud technologies;

- Be a part of cutting-edge, open-source innovation;

- Thrive in the high-energy environment of a young company where openness, collaboration, risk-taking, and continuous growth are valued;

- Professional development and training;

- Attend conferences and working groups;

- Company outings, happy hours, hackathons, and tech talks;

- Receive a competitive compensation package with a strong benefits plan.

Opting out of ADMT use is requested for decisions about evaluation and review connected with the specific employment decision for the position applied for. You also have the right to appeal any decisions made by ADMT by sending your request to isamoylova@mirantis.com

title: Corporate Paralegal
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the Role 

Mistral AI's corporate legal team is looking for a Corporate Paralegal to join our growing legal function in Paris. This is a newly created role designed to centralize and streamline the administrative backbone of our corporate legal operations as we scale internationally.

This is a high-autonomy role. You will own several critical workstreams end-to-end — from KYC and entity housekeeping to cap table management and contract administration — and you will be expected to exercise sound judgment, escalate when needed, and drive automation wherever possible.

What you'll do 

1. Cap Table & Share Register 

Own the cap table across different systems with rigor and precision. Record all share movements — issuances, transfers, ESOP/BSPCE, funding rounds. Maintain the legal share register and reconcile against articles, shareholders' agreements, and board minutes. Produce cap table extracts, shareholder lists, and ownership reports for KYC, audit, board packs, and investors — always under NDA and with judgment on what can be disclosed. Strong Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, reconciliation) are essential.

2. Entity Management, Corporate Formalities & Notarisation 

Handle entity creation from incorporation to corporate maintenance across jurisdictions (SAS, Inc, Ltd, Pte, GmbH, etc.) with confidentiality and attention to detail. Manage the annual formalities calendar, board/shareholder minutes, resolutions, powers of attorney, and the entity housekeeping file for each group company. Coordinate notarial formalities — share transfers, capital changes, statutory modifications, pledges. Handle apostilles, legalisation, and certified translations for documents used abroad via the Legal Vision Platform. Maintain up-to-date KYC packs for each entity: Kbis, articles, directors, beneficial ownership, administrative certificates. Respond to inbound KYC requests from banks, clients, and investors. Log every formalité for a complete and auditable record.

3. Insurance & Document Management 

Manage insurance policies, certificates (COIs), and the renewal calendar. Handle COI requests by checking them against contractual requirements and following up with brokers. Keep a register of policies and claims. File and archive documents with naming conventions and versioning in our document management tools. Manage e-signatures (DocuSign). Maintain the contract register with expiry dates and notice periods. Provide up-to-date insurance certificates and policy summaries as part of KYC documentation for each entity.

4. Procurement Contracts 

First-level review of NDAs, order forms, and simple SOWs against Mistral templates, flagging deviations for escalation. Version comparison and clean redlines. Understand the procurement policy to know when legal review is mandatory. Coordinate with Procurement, business teams, and Finance to move deals to signature. Complete supplier onboarding questionnaires (anti-bribery, sanctions, ESG, security) and supplier portals (Ariba, Coupa) as part of the vendor KYC process. Comfortable with tools like Ironclad, Notion, and Slack; keen to automate and reduce manual work.

What you bring 

- 10+ years of experience in a legal field, with a strong preference for corporate law (M&A, banking, funds, or large corporate groups).

- Experience in a law firm (corporate/M&A/banking), investment fund, bank, or a large multinational group (e.g., CAC 40).

- Proven experience with KYC processes, questionnaires, and administrative certificates.

- Strong understanding of confidentiality, data protection (GDPR), and the judgment to know what can and cannot be shared externally.

- Hands-on experience with cap table management tools (Ledgy, Axiocap) or share register administration.

- Familiarity with French corporate law (SAS) and international entity structures (Delaware Inc, UK Ltd, Singapore Pte, German GmbH).

- Experience with contract lifecycle management (CLM) tools and e-signature platforms.

- Exposure to procurement contract review and vendor onboarding.

- Fluent in English and French (both written and spoken). Additional languages are a plus.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

Privacy Policy 

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

description:

- Strong expertise with containers (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)

- Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and on-premises virtualization (RHEL)

- Solid understanding of networking concepts and protocols, and of security best practices for highly sensitive environments

- Strong presence with customers, from action officers to senior leaders, and clear, concise writing

- Calm under pressure, and focused on forward motion

title: Principal Technical Consultant
description:
About Ping Identity: 

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it. 

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. 

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. 

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. 

As a Professional Services Technical Consultant, you will play a technical role in the architecture and successful installation, integration, and deployment of Identity and Access solutions in our clients' environments. You will also assist our implementation partners in that process. You will report to the Director of Professional Services.

You will: 

- Deliver technical consulting to our customers and partners from various industries including financial services, manufacturing, government, utilities, and more. 

- Evaluate client business, process, systems, and technology requirements and advise clients on best practices to help guide and solidify proposed designs.

- Consult with clients to assess current problem states, establish desired future states, and make solution recommendations.

- Participate in the detailed solution design, implementation, and delivery of Ping Identity IAM product solutions to our clients.

- Work with customers to install, deploy, and configure Ping Identity solutions to meet the customer's requirements.

- Collaborate with Ping Internal teams on escalated customer issues requiring deployment expertise. 

- Participate in services pre-sales processes including presentation of effort size, best practices, and feasibility studies.

- Develop materials for providing technical consulting (e.g., best practices, report templates, delivery guides, knowledge base articles).

- Help partners ensure they design an architecture aligned to Ping best practices for a successful customer deployment.

- Mentor and assist in the development of internal and external technical resources.

- Lead technical delivery from discovery and design through implementation, testing, production readiness, and handover, coordinating dependencies and surfacing delivery risks early.

- Design and validate secure, scalable, highly available IAM deployments across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments, including integration, operational, and disaster-recovery considerations.

- Troubleshoot complex implementation and production issues by analysing logs, traces, configurations, and network behaviour; work with Support and Product Engineering to drive resolution where needed.

- Define and execute technical validation activities, including integration, end-to-end, performance, and resilience testing, and support cutover and go-live planning.

- Produce clear implementation documentation, runbooks, and knowledge-transfer materials so customer and partner teams can operate and support the solution after delivery.

- Balance strong security controls with a seamless user experience when shaping identity journeys and recommendations.

You have: 

- 5+ years of experience working in a consulting capacity with a minimum of 2 years working directly in the Identity and Access Management space within a large organization or enterprise

- Background in a consulting capacity within the Identity and Access Management space, including practical System Integration and Implementation experience 

- A capability-maturity approach to IAM deployments

- Comfortable with subjects such as TCP/IP networking, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, OIDC, LDAP, and Data Stores

- Experience with Java/JavaScript/Groovy, HTML/CSS to support web application development

- Experience in effort estimates and sizing of projects

- Self-motivated, willing to take initiative, organized, able to work unaccompanied, and manage communications appropriately

- Bachelor of Science in a related field (e.g. Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Information Systems) or equivalent work-related level of experience

- Availability to travel up to 50% of the time

- Outstanding cross-functional cooperation skills in particular with our Go-To-Market units.

- Excellent communication, both verbal and written

- Practical experience integrating IAM platforms with enterprise directories, applications, APIs, and identity systems, including federation, authentication, and user lifecycle or provisioning flows.

- Experience with identity standards and protocols such as SCIM, HTTP/REST APIs, and common directory and federation patterns, in addition to OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, OIDC, FIDO and LDAP.

- Experience designing or delivering IAM solutions in cloud, hybrid, or on-premises environments, including deployment, upgrade, resilience, and operational support considerations.

- Strong diagnostic skills across application, identity, and network layers, with experience using logs and traces to isolate and resolve integration issues.

- Experience planning and carrying out technical testing, production cutovers, and transition to customer or partner operations.

- Ability to facilitate technical discovery and design workshops, explain trade-offs clearly, and adapt recommendations to customer constraints and desired outcomes.

- Experience working within structured delivery practices, including managing technical risks, dependencies, decisions, and changes across a customer engagement.

You have an advantage if: 

- Computer and Software Security certifications 

- ForgeRock or Ping training badges/certifications 

- Skills with DevOps best practices, including deployment automation tools, CI/CD, Docker, Terraform, and Kubernetes 

- Experience with Ping Identity products and architectures, such as PingFederate, PingAccess, PingDirectory, PingOne, or PingID.

- Experience with identity governance, privileged access, customer identity, or workforce identity use cases beyond a single IAM product or deployment pattern.

- Familiarity with observability and operational tooling, such as centralised logging, monitoring, alerting, and distributed tracing.

- Experience with source control, infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, and automated testing for repeatable IAM deployments.

- Experience migrating identity services, applications, or user populations from legacy platforms to modern IAM architectures.

Life at Ping: 

We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We're growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that's who we want to succeed with every day. 

Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special: 

- A company culture that empowers you to do your best work.

- Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone.

- Regular company and team bonding events.

- Competitive benefits and perks.

- Global volunteering and community initiatives

Our Benefits: 

- Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule 

- Parental Leave

- Progressive Healthcare Options

- Retirement Programs

- Opportunity for Education Reimbursement 

- Commuter Offset (Specific locations) 

Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone's individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self.

We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Upsun Dispatch, our newest offering, brings that same idea to the whole team. It’s the platform for governed collaboration between AI agents and cross-functional humans. We give you your time back. You get:

The name says it all. “Up” stands for uptime, reliability, and acceleration. “Sun” reflects our follow-the-sun support: a 24x7, globally distributed team keeping the lights on while you rest. We believe software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation. 

Upsunners are a remote, global team, and we thrive in a multicultural one. We’re committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment, and our people span the whole experience spectrum. What ties us together is curiosity, a thirst for knowledge, and an eagerness for new ideas and cultures. Reporting directly to the Chief Marketing Officer, you will own the revenue target for product-led experiences, building a scalable engine across developer recruitment, freemium conversion, and customer retention. Working at the intersection of Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering, you will bridge technical platform capabilities with market-driven execution to scale Upsun’s global footprint.

- 
Drive growth goals: Build and execute PLG programs to achieve clear top-line ARR milestones and hit aggressive user acquisition targets with specific focus in Europe and North America.

- 
Build tight feedback loops: Analyze intent data, user behavior, and churn metrics to continuously iterate on user onboarding, NPS, and lifetime value. 

What you bring 

- 
PLG and growth leadership: A track record as a Senior Product Manager or Director with growth and commercial revenue responsibilities at a developer-focused, SaaS, or cloud platform company driven primarily by a PLG model. 

- 
Strategic judgment: Ability to turn complex developer platform capabilities into intuitive self-service user experiences that drive clear, measurable business value. 

- 
Cross-functional execution: A record of leading cross-functional growth initiatives across Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering. 

- 
Data-driven approach: Hands-on depth in growth analytics, conversion funnels, freemium-to-paid activation, and retention. 

- 
Developer and AI fluency: Practical understanding of modern developer workflows, cloud infrastructure, and how AI-assisted development tools are reshaping user expectations. 

Bonus points 

- 
Dual-funnel experience: Running both self-serve funnels (PLG) and enterprise sales handoffs (PLS). 

- 
Platform background: Cloud infrastructure, PaaS, DevOps, or developer platforms. 

- 
Global scale: Scaling product-led revenue across remote-first, international teams. 

Where we hire 

At Upsun, remote work isn't just a trend - it's our foundation. The freedom of remote work with the support of a diverse, global team has been our successful model for over a decade. Our culture celebrates flexibility and collaboration, and while we have team members in over 30 countries around the globe, we are currently focused on hiring for this role in Canada, France, Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States . How we hire

What we offer

🏆 An Award-Winning Workplace - We’ve been recognized by Forbes’ Top 30 Companies for Remote Jobs and France’s Best Workplaces for Women. 

🗣️ A culture that values your voice - Join a flexible, open, and inclusive work environment where your voice is encouraged, and your ideas shape our growth and evolution.

title: Senior Software Engineer (AI/Data)
description:
About Codat 

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role 

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform: Codat's client intelligence delivered inside the assistant a banker already uses (Microsoft Copilot first). Ask it anything about a client and it answers from the client's real books. Don't ask, and it still tells you what's changed, why it matters and what to do about it. Under it we're building the semantic layer, so every answer uses the same definitions, the signal layer that spots what's changed for a client, and the reasoning layer, a Codat-side LLM that turns those signals into advice. The first bank goes live this year. You'll be building the data and reasoning behind all of it.

This is a hands-on job for software engineers who want to build the systems a model reasons over, not configure a warehouse. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS. The product lives inside the AI assistant our clients already use, and we build it the same way: agents do the repetitive work, engineers do the hard parts. You'll build it and you'll run it. Nobody hands it over the wall once it's live. You'll also get a real say in where it goes next. That means making your case to engineers, product and the commercial team, and bringing them along with you.

What You'll Work On 

- The semantic layer. Measures, dimensions and definitions the model is allowed to use, so every answer it gives is the same answer. Yours to grow, persona by persona.

- The signal layer. Detecting what's changed for a client and surfacing it before the banker asks. You'll be designing and building this.

- The reasoning layer. A Codat-side LLM that turns signals into advice. Our calculations are the ground truth it reasons over. You own the calculations the model relies on, and the names, definitions and structure that let it pick the right one.

- The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. What tools it has, how they're built, how they fail, and the evals that prove they work.

- Everything from raw source data to the number the assistant quotes: the pipelines, services and data models, with the testing and observability to prove the number is right and the evals that catch the model quoting the wrong one.

You'll Probably Have 

- Built production systems from scratch, writing the code yourself rather than configuring managed services. You think about interfaces, failure modes and how the next person will change your code. If we ask about the hardest system you've built, you'll have a story ready.

- Served data to an LLM and seen where it goes wrong: ambiguous definitions, poor retrieval, no evals. You know why "the model will work it out" isn't a data strategy.

- Worked with data along the way, and liked it. You may never have been called a data engineer. You've built things that move, shape and serve data, and you know how they break, and how a model breaks on top of them.

- Solid C#, Python or another backend language. Your code comes with tests, and you leave things tidier than you found them.

- Depth in at least one of SQL, Spark, Databricks/Delta Lake, Dagster/Airflow/Temporal or dbt. Bonus if you've shaped any of them into something a model can query, through a metrics layer, metric views or an MCP server.

- Time with CI/CD, Docker, cloud infrastructure (we're on Azure) and observability. Even better if you set them up for a team.

- An interest in the business behind the data. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you'll say so, and you'll build the guard-rail so the model says so too.

- Treated your own workflow as something to engineer. AI has already taken over the repetitive parts of it, and you're the person others ask how to do the same.

How We Work 

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There’s no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don’t want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

Compensation: £90K – £110K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Software Engineer - (Home Energy)
description:
About Enode 

The grid was built for predictable, centralised power. Today it's absorbing intermittent supply from grid scale solar and wind, alongside dynamic demand from EVs, heat pumps, and home batteries. The missing piece is software that can connect and orchestrate these devices at scale.

Enode provides the infrastructure layer that makes this possible. Our Connect API gives energy companies a single integration to 1000+ devices across 80+ brands. Our optimisation tooling gives energy companies the building blocks to manage those devices locally - think smart charging for EVs. Our Flex product turns those connected devices into a flexible, controllable asset for energy companies.

We work with device manufacturers across the energy hardware ecosystem - from EV brands to heat pump and solar inverter producers. Our customers are energy retailers, utilities, and traders building the next generation of energy services. We're backed by Y Combinator, Lowercarbon Capital, and Creandum.

The decisions made now will shape how the energy system gets built. We're looking for people who take ownership, move fast, and care deeply about the role technology can play in the energy transition.

What we're looking for:

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to help build the software layer that makes home energy devices work as one system. The Home Energy team owns Enode's integrations and APIs for batteries, solar inverters, HVAC, and smart meters, along with the home energy management (HEM) system and statistics that customers build on. You'll build integrations with leading OEMs and help mature our API surface into the unified control layer for the home, at a moment when customer demand for battery and home energy optimization is accelerating.

You'll join the Home Energy team, reporting to the team's Engineering Manager. You'll collaborate closely with your PM, fellow backend engineers, and our partnership and commercial teams, from assessing OEM API feasibility to shaping how customers control energy assets through our platform.

In this role, you will:

- Build and maintain integrations with OEM cloud platforms across batteries, solar, smart meters, and HVAC.

- Design and evolve our home energy APIs, unifying telemetry and controls across HEM system, batteries, and curtailment into a product surface customers can build optimizations on.

- Improve observability and vendor performance across our integrations, and take part in the team's triage rotation.

- Work with partnership and commercial teams on API feasibility for new OEM integrations.

- Build strong relationships with the customers who rely on our platform, working alongside your PM and commercial partners, and let what you learn from them shape what we build.

- Debug and ship production features in Node/TypeScript on our AWS-based stack.

- Take a product-engineer mindset, balancing speed, quality, and customer impact in your day-to-day decisions.

Curious what you'd actually be building? Explore our API docs and the Enode Tech Blog to see what we ship and how we think about it.

This role will be right for you, if:

You're an ambitious backend engineer who likes to own things end to end: from an ambiguous problem, through design and integration work, to something shipped and running in production. You find integration challenges satisfying rather than frustrating, including working with third-party APIs of varying maturity, and you're energized by tough technical problems.

You're comfortable navigating ambiguity and bringing clarity and structure that help a team move forward. You collaborate naturally with engineers, PMs, and commercial partners, and you like being close enough to the product to influence where it goes.

Above all, you care about building software with real-world impact that supports the shift toward a cleaner, more flexible energy system. You bring: 

- Experience building and maintaining backend services in production, ideally in API or integration-heavy systems.

- Strong skills in designing for reliability, scalability, and performance.

- Ability to own work from initial scoping to production rollout, including iterating based on customer or usage insights.

- Comfort in fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environments where teams create clarity together.

- Clear, thoughtful communication across engineering, product, and customer-facing teams.

- A product mindset: you care about solving the right problem and making life easier for customers and teammates.

Nice to have:

- Experience with TypeScript/Node, AWS services, PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, or similar production tooling.

- Familiarity with home energy assets (batteries, solar/inverters, HVAC, smart meters), energy markets, or IoT/device ecosystems.

- Prior exposure to API-first products or integration platforms.

- On-call or incident response experience.

What we offer:

- Opportunity to join and impact an early-stage climate tech startup with global aspirations as we scale.

- A mission-driven, fun and caring environment with high drive and ambition.

- Competitive compensation, including a very attractive employee option program - you’re part of our journey.

- Access to best in class AI tooling, we think the ceiling on what a small team can do has fundamentally shifted, and we want you to feel that.

- Remote-first in Europe, with the option of attending an office in Oslo or receiving a co-working pass on demand.

- Three annual off-sites to connect with the team in exciting & fun places.

- Flexible, human-first culture.

- Stipend for setting up your home office.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A few things to note:

- Enode is an equal opportunities employer. Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of colour are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles.

- Our values are integral to the way we work and are embedded into all our hiring processes. You can read more about our values here .

title: Machine Learning Engineer - IV (Biometrics)
description:

Role Purpose 

We’re looking for a Staff/Senior Machine Learning Engineer with deep expertise in computer vision and biometrics to lead the design and scaling of face recognition systems in production. You’ll build and train models, and own ML systems end-to-end on AWS. The final job level for this role will be determined following the interview process.

What You’ll Do 

Lead the design and development of computer vision systems for biometrics (face attributes, detection, quality, and recognition)
Rigorous fairness analysis and benchmarking of biometric models across various datasets and operating conditions.
Architect, train, and optimize models using PyTorch, Tensorflow, and/or JAX
Own and evolve end-to-end ML pipelines, from data ingestion to deployment. Design automated pipelines (Airflow) for data ingestion and cleaning. You will be responsible for curating balanced training sets and generating synthetic data to address both quality and diversity gaps.
Production Engineering: Own the path to production. Optimize models for low-latency inference (quantization, distillation, TensorRT/ONNX) and manage deployment on AWS.
Mentor ML engineers, conduct code/design reviews, and drive technical best practices across the Computer Vision team.

What We’re Looking For 

Experience: 5+ years of industry experience in Machine Learning, with at least 3 years dedicated to Biometrics or Face Analysis.
Deep expertise in computer vision and biometrics, especially face recognition.
Fairness & Ethics: You understand the sources of algorithmic bias in Computer Vision and have practical experience measuring and mitigating disparate impact.
Strong Engineering: Expert proficiency in Python (both machine learning and vision libraries such as Pillow, OpenCV, PyTorch, etc). You write clean, modular, production-ready code.
Systems Architecture: Experience designing end-to-end ML pipelines (Data to Train to Deploy) and working with workflow orchestrators like Airflow.
Cloud Native: Hands-on experience scaling training jobs on multi-GPU clusters and deploying services on AWS (SageMaker, EC2, EKS).

Nice to Have 

Research Publications: Papers in CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, or FG related to face recognition, image quality assessment, or fairness.
Large Scale Search: Experience with vector databases (e.g., Milvus, Faiss) and approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search algorithms.
Familiarity with privacy, security, and compliance in biometric systems.
Mobile/Edge Experience: Experience porting models to edge or mobile devices utilizing frameworks such as CoreML, LiteRT, and/or TFLite.
Synthetic Data: Experience using GANs or diffusion models to generate synthetic faces for training.
Strong communication skills.

Jumio Values: 

IDEAL: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation 

Equal Opportunities : 

Jumio is a collaboration of people with different ideas, strengths, interests and cultures. We welcome applications and colleagues from all backgrounds and of all statuses.

Jumio is a B2B technology company dedicated to eradicating online identity fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes to help make the internet safer. Jumio is the leading provider of online identity verification, eKYC and AML solutions. With a global footprint, we’re expanding the team to meet strong client demand across a range of industries including Financial Services, Travel, Sharing Economy, Fintech, Gaming, and others.

title: AI Product Engineer
description:
What is Finary? 

We are on a mission to give power back to investors . Great financial guidance has always existed, it just came with a minimum net worth. We're changing that by building the AI-powered one-stop shop for investing, where you can track your assets, manage your budget, invest, and learn. One simple, ambitious idea drives us: put a private banker in everyone's pocket.

Mounir launched Finary in 2021, and more than 1,000,000 people now trust us with their financial lives. We ship cutting-edge products with touches of delight, and we care deeply about experience, performance, and ease of use.

Why now? 

A new generation of investors is emerging: ambitious, involved, done with taboos around money. We see a world where investing empowers everybody to live the life they've always dreamt of. To fuel that, we raised €40M from Hedosophia, Y Combinator, and Speedinvest, alongside founders and operators like Steve Anavi & Alexandre Prot (Qonto), Matthieu Rouif (Photoroom), Eric Demuth (Bitpanda), Axel Weber (former UBS Chairman), and Harsh Sinha (CTO at Wise).

In July 2026, the AMF granted us our MiCA license, on top of our Investment Firm license: one of the very few French platforms holding both, offering stocks, ETFs and crypto on a single regulated platform, right as Europe consolidates around licensed players. There's never been a more exciting time to join.

What we offer 

We're 70 builders who genuinely love what they do: real ownership from day one, tier-1 salary and equity, offices in the heart of Paris with hybrid remote, and quarterly gatherings we actually look forward to.

We hire A-players who are as kind as they are demanding, people whose ideas transform not just our product but the way we work and think. Our culture is direct, transparent, and built on radical candor: we challenge each other openly, then commit. And we don't hedge on AI. It's the single most important skill of the next decade and a real bar here. Everyone at Finary has rebuilt how they work around it. If that's already second nature to you, you'll be surrounded by people pushing that frontier every day.

Read more about our values here .

The opportunity

AI is not a side project at Finary: it's how we intend to run the company. Our teams already build their own automations, so this role is about the hard part: complex orchestrations, and intelligence inside the products our advisors and operations team rely on every day. You own what you build end to end, from understanding the need with the people who'll use it to running it in production. We move fast and need an AI product engineer to move with us.

What you'll do

- Advisory at scale : build the closing machine and the systems that accelerate our sales team

- Allocation engines : build the recommendation engine that captures our advisors' expertise

- Operating systems : build the agentic layer that lets our operations team orchestrate a fleet of AI agents, with minimal humans interactions

- End-to-end ownership : gather needs with the teams who use your products, then design, build, deploy and maintain them; define what a correct agent decision looks like, measure it, and catch drift before users do

- Enablement : help non-engineers build their own automations, step in when they need something more robust, and work with the rest of engineering on shared agentic infrastructure

What we're looking for

- Production software experience : 3+ years shipping production grade software, including products you've owned end to end, from gathering needs to running them

- AI systems in production : you've built and run LLM integrations, agents and multi-step orchestrations in production. You can explain how they work and evaluate them. You know when a simple rule beats an agent, and AI coding tools are part of your daily work.

- Range across the stack : comfortable across several languages and codebases, and quick to pick up new ones. Our stack is TypeScript, Rust and Ruby, on Google Cloud and Kubernetes with infrastructure as code. You don't need to be an SRE, but you deploy and run what you build and keep data correct as systems evolve

- Product sense and UX : you start from the problem, not the technology, and you care about the people using what you build and how it feels to use

- High agency : you work across teams and switch context often, and you find the next problem worth solving and own it without waiting to be told

- French and English : fluent French to work with our advisory team and the rest of the company, and professional English

- Based in Western Europe : we expect quarterly presence for our onsite weeks in Paris

- We're particularly interested in:

- An agentic system you built that is in production and used today

- How you know it works, and what it saves the people using it

- A time you chose a simple script or rule over an agent, and why

Nice to have

- Familiarity with fintech or a regulated industry

- Passion for personal finance and investing

What we offer

- Competitive salary: €65k - €80k base depending on experience, plus stock options

- Hybrid setup : teammates across France and Europe, with one week together in Paris every quarter (travel and accommodation covered)

- Closeness to your users : you're part of the Operations team, work across advisory, sales, operations and engineering, and have direct access to the people using what you build from day one

- High-performing environment : A-players who challenge you and help you grow

- Impact that compounds : what you build today makes every team more effective tomorrow

title: FPGA Firmware Engineer
description:
About Singular Photonics:

Singular Photonics is a fast-growing fabless semiconductor start-up, developing Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) sensors that bring advanced computation directly into imaging. Our sensors enable innovations across LiDAR, fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM), spectroscopy and time-resolved optical measurements, powering next-generation solutions for customers worldwide. Based at Orchard Brae House in Edinburgh, we are a close-knit team at the forefront of the photonics revolution.

About the Role:

We are seeking an FPGA Firmware Engineer to join our multidisciplinary R&D team. This is an FPGA role: you will design, implement and verify the Verilog firmware that powers our SPAD sensors, captures photon timing data at high rates and streams it to the host.

Our sensors generate data faster than most imaging systems ever see, so the interesting problems here are real ones: clock domain crossing, timing closure and getting data off the device without losing a photon. You will work alongside our hardware, ASIC and software engineers, from architecture through to system bring-up and customer deployment.

You will report to the Lead Firmware Engineer.

Key Responsibilities:

- Architecture: Define FPGA requirements and architecture for SPAD sensor readout, in discussion with the hardware, ASIC and software teams.
- RTL Design: Implement, verify and debug Verilog modules for data acquisition, photon timing, histogramming and sensor control.
- Verification: Design and run simulations and testbenches, with coverage sufficient to trust the design before it reaches hardware.
- Synthesis & Timing: Own synthesis, constraints, clock domain crossing and timing closure on AMD-Xilinx FPGA family devices in Vivado.
- High-Speed Interfaces: Build and integrate the high-speed interfaces that move sensor data: PCIe, USB3, Ethernet, AXI interface, MIPI, LVDS, SLVS, Camera Link.
- Bring-Up & Debug: Lead firmware bring-up on new boards and sensors, debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analysers and in-system probes.
- Source Control & Build: Keep RTL under version control with a repeatable, automated build, and document designs to the standard our ISO 9001 design control process requires.
- Reviews & Support: Contribute to design reviews, and support the software team and customers during field integration.
Experience & Skills:

Essential:

- Strong proficiency in Verilog, and a solid grounding in RTL design, synthesis and timing closure.
- Hands-on experience with AMD-Xilinx Vivado and its toolchain.
- Experience writing your own testbenches and verifying a design in simulation before hardware.
- Experience bringing up firmware on real hardware and debugging it in the lab.
- Experience with at least one high-speed interface or bus at RTL level.
- Comfortable in a small company where priorities shift and everyone pitches in.
- Working with complex, existing codebases and seamlessly integrating new functionality with minimal disruption.
Desirable:

- SystemVerilog, and verification practices beyond directed testbenches.
- Comfortable working in Linux operating systems.
- Exposure to any of PCIe, AXI interface, USB3, Ethernet, MIPI, LVDS, SLVS or Camera Link.
- C, C++ or Python for embedded software integration and test automation.
- Experience with image sensors, time-of-flight, TDCs or single-photon detection.
- Familiarity with PCB design tools such as Altium Designer, and reading schematics during debug.
Educational Background:

- Degree in Electronics Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- 2-5 years' experience in FPGA and digital design.
Key Attributes & Behaviours:

- Rigour: Disciplined about verification - you would rather find it in simulation than on the bench.
- Debugging: Systematic when the fault could be in the RTL, the board or the sensor, and comfortable with the instruments that tell you which.
- Clarity: Writes documentation and code that colleagues can pick up without you in the room.
- Collaboration: Works well across the hardware, ASIC and software boundaries rather than only inside the FPGA.
- Ownership: Takes a problem from architecture through to a working system, and sees it through.
- Adaptability: Comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment where the requirement can move.
Success Indicators:

- Firmware that meets timing and functions correctly on first hardware more often than not, with issues found in simulation rather than on the bench.
- Effective bring-up and debugging support during prototype validation and customer deployment, with hardware and firmware issues resolved promptly.
- Design documentation, simulation coverage and design review contributions good enough for another engineer to maintain the work.
Benefits of Joining Singular Photonics

At Singular Photonics, we are committed to fostering a rewarding and supportive environment for our team. As an FPGA Firmware Engineer, you will benefit from:

- Pension: 5% company contribution.
- Share Options: Participation in the Company EMI Share Option Scheme, so you share in the growth you help build.
- Enhanced Annual Leave: 35 days paid annual leave per year, inclusive of UK public holidays.
- Hybrid Working: Primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week (full time worker).
- Career Growth: Work on silicon and systems few engineers get near, with the chance to shape how we do FPGA development as the team grows.
- Additional Benefits: [Cycle to work and private medical insurance (once implemented)
Why Join Us

This position offers a rare opportunity to work at the forefront of SPAD sensor technology, driving innovation and shaping future applications in photonics and imaging. At Singular Photonics you will be part of a passionate, close-knit team, where the work you do is visible in the product and in the hands of customers.

Location & Work Environment

Based at Orchard Brae House, Queensferry Road, Edinburgh. This is a full-time, permanent role. The work is hands-on with hardware in our lab, so it is primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week.

Right to work in the UK is essential. We are unfortunately unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

iwoca launched its business credit card in 2026. It gives small businesses a fast, flexible way to pay for what they need and control their cash flow, alongside iwoca’s loans. The card is a core part of iwoca’s long-term growth.

The Payments infrastructure team builds iwoca’s card payments platform. Its job is to approve each payment in moments when a customer uses their card. The team also builds the platforms that pay out rewards as customers spend and monitor every transaction.

The team is small – a principal engineer, a product manager with a background in payments, and you. It works closely with iwoca’s ledger, fraud and customer product teams.

The role 

As a senior backend engineer, you’ll own services and projects end to end, and shape the platform’s architecture with the principal engineer, from service boundaries to how authorisation, rewards, and transaction monitoring fit together. You’ll work closely with product to decide what the team builds and how. There’s still plenty to build, and you’ll take new services into production.

You’ll build on your payments expertise alongside the principal engineer, with scope to grow as the platform matures. Most of the challenge is technical: scaling payments within card scheme rules and the regulation iwoca has to meet. Your code will run every time a small business uses its iwoca card.

Live project examples:

- Payment authorisation. Extending the service built to approve or decline each card payment in real time, using data held in other services. It places a hold on available credit in the ledger and applies iwoca's own checks, such as account status, merchant category code restrictions, and spend limits.

- Transaction monitoring. Building the service that will screen card transactions for fraud and financial-crime risk as customers spend, so iwoca will rely less on third parties.

- Rewards. Extending the service that pays out cashback, as the team adds to what the card offers.

- Testing for failure. Designing sandbox tests that cover edge cases and failures across the card transaction lifecycle.

- Ledger cutover and go-live. Moving the card platform onto iwoca's own ledger and infrastructure with as little downtime as possible, then fixing the issues that only show up in production.

The requirements 

Essential:

- Payment systems. You've designed and run highly available, low-latency payment systems in production, ideally on the issuing side.

- Card payment flows. You've worked on card authorisation and clearing, and traced transactions from the terminal, through the acquirer and card scheme, to the issuer. You've used response codes to diagnose declined transactions.

- Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You've written and run backend services in it.

- Distributed systems. You've built microservices, REST APIs, and asynchronous messaging with queues or topics, and designed the database schemas behind them, ideally in PostgreSQL.

- AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

- Ledgers and clearing. You've worked on a ledger, reconciliation, or clearing system – for cards, loyalty points, bank transfers, or money remittance.

- Testing. You've written automated tests for payment systems, ideally test-first.

- Python. You've used Python in production. It's the language the team works in.

The salary 

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £120,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture 

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

title: Field Integration Engineer
description:
Applied Intuition , Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co .

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions 

About the Role 

We are seeking Field Integration Engineers who excel at connecting software engineering, customer interaction, and hands-on field operations. In this position, you will drive the full-stack integration and deployment of our software solutions across customer hardware, physical vehicles, and test benches.

Serving as the key technical expert on-site, mainly in the great Chicago area, you will ensure our software operates seamlessly on customer vehicles. You will bring up target hardware, SIL, and HIL setups; troubleshoot integration challenges spanning software, firmware, and vehicle networks; and partner directly with customer systems and software engineering teams to deliver production-ready autonomous and intelligent vehicle technology.

Travel Expectation: This position requires significant travel (30%–50%+) to customer facilities, proving grounds, test tracks, and active field deployment sites.

At Applied Intuition, you will: 

- 
Deploy, configure, and integrate vehicle software stack, middleware, and application-level code on customer target hardware, HIL simulators, and vehicle platforms.

- 
Serve as the primary technical escalation point on-site. Collect logs/telemetry, bisect software pipelines, debug system crashes, and isolate root causes across software-hardware boundaries.

- 
Debug and validate communication interfaces (CAN, LIN, Automotive Ethernet, J1939) and verify end-to-end data flow between sensors, ECUs, and application software.

- 
Partner closely with internal core software/firmware engineering teams to reproduce complex field issues, validate fixes, and push continuous system improvements.

- 
Write Python scripts, Bash automation, and internal tooling to streamline deployment, automated diagnostics, and log collection in field environments.

- 
Work directly with customer engineering leadership to define target integration use-cases, articulate system constraints, and establish clear integration milestones.

We're looking for someone who has: 

- 
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

- 
Strong programming skills in embedded C and/or C++, with solid software engineering practices in Linux development and command-line environments.

- 
2+ years of hands-on experience integrating, testing, and debugging software applications on physical target platforms or embedded hardware.

- 
Practical understanding of automotive or industrial network topologies, protocol analysis (CAN, Ethernet, J1939), and diagnostic standards (UDS, DoIP, OBD-II).

- 
Strong analytical skills to systematically isolate faults across multi-component software pipelines and hardware interfaces.

- 
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the confidence to represent the engineering team in fast-paced, high-stakes customer environments.

- 
Ability and willingness to travel 30%–50%+ to domestic and international customer locations and testing sites.

Nice to have: 

- 
Experience with vehicle platforms, autonomous systems, robotics, or active industrial/field environments.

- 
Familiarity with AUTOSAR platform concepts (RTE, SWCs, ARXML), SIL/HIL test rigs, or ROS/ROS2 architecture.

- 
Experience using network analysis tools (e.g., Vector CANoe/CANape, Wireshark, PEAK-System) or hardware debugging tools (oscilloscopes, multimeters).

- 
Scripting capability in Python for data processing, log parsing, or test automation.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Software Engineer AI Coding Tasks
description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works 

- Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
- Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
- Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
- Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
- Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
- Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
- Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements 

- 2+ years of professional software engineering
- Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
- Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
- Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
- Regular use of an AI coding tool
- Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
- You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
- At least 10 hours a week, starting now
- A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

Nice to have 

- Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
- Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms 

- US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
- Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
- The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
- Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer
