title: Principal Infrastructure Engineer
description:
500M+ downloads. 80M+ monthly users. A decade of building – and we’re still accelerating. 

Flo is the world’s #1 health & fitness app worldwide on a mission to build a better future for female health. Backed by a $200M investment led by General Atlantic, we became the first product of our kind to reach a $1B valuation in 2024 – and we’re not slowing down.

With 7M paid subscribers and the highest-rated experience in the App Store’s health category, we’ve spent 10 years earning trust at scale. Now, we’re building the next generation of digital health – AI-powered, privacy-first, clinically backed – to help our users know their body better.

The job 

Principal Infrastructure Engineer 

More than 80 million women open Flo every month to understand their bodies and their health. Every one of those sessions runs on infrastructure we build, and the data behind it is as personal as data gets. Keeping that fast and private at this scale is the job.

Velocity runs the platform that every Flo engineer builds on: Kubernetes on AWS, the data stores behind our services, and the golden paths that let product teams ship without needing to be infrastructure experts. We treat our internal developers as our customers. You will:

- Own the foundations: Design and run the Kubernetes and data infrastructure behind 80 million monthly active users, and make it boring in the best sense.

- Turn expertise into self-service: Take what you know about running clusters and databases well, and build it into the defaults so product teams get it for free.

What You Will Do 

- Kubernetes at scale: Architect and evolve our EKS estate: cluster lifecycle and upgrades, networking, autoscaling, workload isolation, and the Helm and Terraform that deploy onto it.

- Data infrastructure: Shape how our services use PostgreSQL, DynamoDB and Kafka. Set the patterns for provisioning, access, backup, failover and capacity, so teams aren't solving these problems one service at a time.

- Golden paths: Build self-service tooling and Terraform modules that give product teams autonomy without sacrificing stability or security.

- Reliability: Lead resilience work, including business continuity planning, disaster recovery testing and a sustainable on-call rotation.

- Privacy at scale: Support the infrastructure behind privacy features such as our TIME-recognised "Anonymous Mode", and keep us SOC2, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified while handling some of the most sensitive data there is.

- Observability: Make sure metrics, logs and traces tell us something is wrong before our users do.

What You Bring 

- Experience: Many years in infrastructure, platform, SRE or DevOps roles running high-traffic, distributed systems in production. You have operated at Principal or Staff scope, setting direction across teams as well as delivering.

- Kubernetes depth: You have run Kubernetes in production for real workloads, ideally EKS. You can explain what happens between kubectl apply and a pod serving traffic, and you have debugged it when it didn't.

- Data infrastructure awareness: You understand how PostgreSQL, DynamoDB and Kafka behave under load and when they fail: connection limits, replication lag, hot partitions, consumer lag, retention. You don't need to have been a DBA, but you know what good looks like and when to ask for help.

- AWS and infrastructure as code: Strong AWS knowledge and fluent Terraform. Coding experience in Go or Python is a plus.

- Communication: A doc-first habit, and the ability to bring distributed product teams with you.

AI first: you will have seen the impact AI automation is having on development teams and the software delivery lifecycle, and have strong ideas on how infrastructure should support it. 

Bonus Points 

- Hardening infrastructure for high-compliance or security-sensitive environments (HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI).

- Running managed data services in AWS (RDS, Aurora, MSK, DynamoDB) at scale, including migrations and major version upgrades.

- Scaling consumer platforms with millions of concurrent users.

- Certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect Professional, CKA or CKS.

Why Join Flo? 

- High impact: Flo is used by 1 in 4 women aged 18–44 in the US, and has raised $200M to build what comes next.

- Autonomy: We hire experts and trust them to deliver.

- Modern stack at scale: EKS, Terraform, Kafka, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB and Sentry, serving more than 80 million people a month.

Annual Salary Range (ranges may vary based on skills and experience)

£130,000 — £150,000 GBP 

How we work 

We’re a mission-led, product-driven team. We move fast, stay focused and take ownership – from brief to build to impact. Debate is encouraged. Decisions are shared. We care about craft, ship with purpose, and always raise the bar.

You’ll be working with people who take their work seriously, not themselves. It takes commitment, resilience, and the drive to keep going when things get tough. Because better health outcomes are worth it. 

What you'll get 

We support impact with meaningful reward. Here’s what that looks like:

- Competitive salary and annual reviews

- Opportunity to participate in Flo’s performance incentive scheme

- Paid holiday, sick leave, and female health leave

- Enhanced parental leave and pay for maternity, paternity, same-sex and adoptive parents

- Accelerated professional growth through world-changing work and learning support

- In-person collaboration and work in a hybrid model, with 3 days per week spent in the office

- 5-week fully paid sabbatical at 5-year Floversary

- Flo Premium for friends & family, plus more health, pension and wellbeing perks

Diversity, equity and inclusion 

Our strength is in our differences. At Flo, hiring is based on merit, skill and what you bring to the role – nothing else. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, communities and identities. Read our privacy notice for job applicants .

title: Product Manager
description:
Wanna join the adventure? 

At Loft, we are convinced that space programs should not have to be rebuilt from scratch every time. Our philosophy has been to productize them: we develop our own proprietary technology blocks, hardware and software, so that a customer payload can be integrated faster and more reliably than any bespoke program allows. That approach has delivered — it is why our customers reach orbit in months rather than years, and it is what makes working here different from working in the rest of the industry.

We are now taking the next step: launching and operating our own constellations, and building a new set of services on top of them. That includes a full product suite enabling third-party AI applications to run directly onboard our satellites, and a growing ecosystem of partners whose needs we have to understand and design for. Loft is expanding at a very high pace, and the range of what we build is expanding just as fast.

This is why Product Management matters so much here. Someone has to hold the whole picture — what is technically possible, what customers actually need, what we should build first — and turn it into something engineering and leadership can act on. As a Product Manager, you will own a significant perimeter and the autonomy that goes with it. We are growing the team precisely so that each of us can go deeper on our topics, anticipate rather than react, and have more impact across the company.

You will need to be comfortable talking to anyone here. In the same week you might sit with a system engineer to understand a design constraint, join a BD call with an institutional customer, and present a recommendation to the executive team. Ideas at Loft get discussed openly and on their merits, wherever they come from, so being able to ask a naive question without ego — and to disagree with someone senior without making it personal — matters more than seniority.

About this role: 
Understand what is possible, and turn it into requirements 

- Spend the bulk of your time with engineering: understanding architectures, constraints, and dependencies well enough to judge what is realistically doable in a given timeframe.

- Translate strategic direction into clear requirements and use cases that engineering can act on directly, and follow them down to the Jira tickets.

- Surface and shape the good ideas that come from engineering — many of the best ones do — and connect them to a product rationale.

- Define success criteria for each capability, and verify they are actually met through implementation and delivery.

- Maintain an accurate, shared view of Loft's product capabilities, what is in development, and where the gaps are.

Bring the outside in 

- Run customer discovery interviews alongside business development, and debrief missions to see how Loft's capabilities are actually used in operations.

- Engage directly with the partners building on our platform, including the onboard AI application ecosystem, to understand their needs and constraints.

- Track market trends and competitive moves closely enough to know where our offering stands.

Decide and prioritize 

- Own the roadmap for your perimeter, reconciling customer needs, engineering reality, and Loft's strategy into a single coherent plan.

- Build the analysis behind every recommendation — sizing, segmentation, business cases, operational data — so decisions are grounded in evidence rather than intuition alone.

- Negotiate scope and delivery commitments with engineering leadership, and re-plan when capacity or mission timelines shift.

- Challenge, constructively and with data, business development, engineering leadership, and your own assumptions.

Communicate 

- Own internal communication on your perimeter: keep engineering, program leadership, and executives working from the same technical reality.

- Develop the technical narratives and proof points that marketing and BD then turn into their own customer-facing material.

- Prepare recommendations and presentations for top-executive-level audiences.

Must Haves: 

- 7+ years of professional experience, including hands-on product management.

- Domain experience in at least one of: earth observation, embedded systems, aerospace systems, security & defense.

- Comfort at both ends of the spectrum — understand the market, and the technology

- Structured and data-driven: you bring your experience and your intuitions, but when you put a recommendation on the table you can show the analysis it stands on.

- Real product obsession: you think about the bigger picture and product-market fit before you think about features.

- Relentless curiosity. In a single month you might move from a satellite bus constraint, to onboard AI inference, to a defense accreditation requirement — and you need to find that stimulating rather than exhausting.

- High autonomy and a bias for action: handed a broad perimeter, you organize it yourself and come back with a plan.

- At ease being challenged, and challenging others, in a fast-moving and demanding environment.

- Working knowledge of both hardware and software development lifecycles.

- Proficient using and configuring Atlassian tools (Jira and Confluence).

- Fluency in English, written and spoken.

- Willingness to travel to other Loft offices and to customers.

Nice to Haves: 

- Fluency in French.

- Experience with AI/ML products, edge computing, or developer and partner platforms and ecosystems.

- Experience with satellite operations, constellation services, or ground segment products.

- Exposure to institutional and defense customers and their procurement cycles.

- Experience in a fast-growing, entrepreneurial NewSpace company or venture-backed deep-tech startup.

- Professional experience working with international teams across time zones.

Some of Our Awesome Benefits: 

- Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success

- Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best

- Health and life insurance, we care about your health

- Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand )

- Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences

- Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together

- Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions. We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes. 

Who We Are 

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit. 

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives. 

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure. 

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

description:
About Nebius : 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Product 

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible. We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role 

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the rendering infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on loading modern web pages in a browser that we patch and build ourselves, so that content is rendered completely and reliably at a cost that works across billions of pages. You will work inside Chromium to remove what we do not need, make the rest faster and cheaper, and keep our build current as Chromium moves. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to 

- Change Chromium in its heavy core (Blink, the V8 integration, the compositor, the network service) to cut CPU, memory and startup cost per page

- Strip Chromium down for agent workloads: skip what nobody needs, such as image and media decoding, web font downloads, and rasterization and GPU work where no one needs pixels, while keeping what page scripts depend on to run correctly (style, layout, animation frames, observers), and work out what breaks, or renders differently, when you do

- Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render

- Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling

- Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you 

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser 

- Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)

- Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service

- Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems 

- Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs

- Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management

- Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with 

- Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine

- Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for

- Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol

- Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)

- Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on 

- Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?

- Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?

- A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?

- Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?

- Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

title: Security Architect
description:
Are you a security specialist in the OT space looking to expand your expertise into cloud solutions? Are you a cloud security champion passionate about bringing your expertise into OT/IoT space? At Priva Product Development Organisation we are looking for the Security Architect who will shape the security of our products. 

  

Security Architect in Priva Product Development – Why this role matters 

At Priva, we develop hardware products and software services for horticulture and building automation. Seeing the importance of our products for our customers, we recognize the need to continuously keep these secure in the ever evolving, fast-paced world. The security requirements in our landscape span four different areas: 

- Physical/embedded device security. 

- OT (operational technology) network security. 

- OT network to Priva-hosted cloud services communications. 

- Priva's hybrid on-prem/multi-cloud platform applications security, including applications, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines. 

What makes this role truly unique is that our products contain long-lived hardware components that our customers run for years. Engineering future-proofed security solutions and maintaining a security posture at existing sites across all these areas having wide range of varying implementations and security needs creates a great challenge and a great fun. 

As part of the architecture team, you will play a key role in shaping the future of Priva's portfolio offered on the global market. You define security standards, security practices and security designs for our products that are used in tens of thousands of buildings and greenhouses. You work across product, engineering, and operations teams to ensure security controls and adhered to, implemented and tested as you have designed these. That’s real impact. 

What you will be doing 

As a Security Architect, you have a very simple mission: you see to it that Priva's hardware products and software (cloud) services are secured against known and emergent threats in lines with the industry standards and practices. You build upon your strong background in securing device/OT networks, cloud applications, and engraining the security practices in the daily work of Agile teams to achieve consistent security posture across all Priva products, designs, and customer deployments. 

 As a security architect, you are trusted counterpart of Priva Security, Quality, and Compliance officer to define, review, and execute controls arising from ISO9001 and ISO27001 standards and internal initiatives. You are responsible for presenting the necessary evidence of Priva’s compliance with these controls to the auditors. 

- Security standards, policies, and design patterns library 

- Security architecture review process 

- Risk register and residual risk acceptance documentation 

- Periodic product security implementation reviews, including maintaining non-compliance register 

- Defined requirements, products and work packages for security-focused projects with 3rd party service providers, reviewing and accepting their deliverables, and supervising the implementation of these deliverables in the Priva hardware products and software services. 

- Regulatory compliance (IEC 62443-4, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 or other standard that may be applicable in specific geographies) 

- Threat intelligence briefing relevant to OT/IoT threat landscape 

- Designing, implementing, and reviewing security controls applied at major customer sites. 

Above all, this is a hands-on role – occasionally writing code is included. You connect the industry’s best practices, ISO standards, product vision with the daily work of the product team. As a security architect, you practice what you preach. You explain, coach, and show by example the implementation of security as Secure SDLC in the developer’s daily work. 

To succeed in this role: 

- You are passionate about OT security; you have great interest in the application of our products in the field. You are curious to grasp how our products truly work for our customers to find the best balance between security, reliability, and cost. You share the opinion that "if I don't secure Priva’s applications, then no one else will". 

- You identify and eliminate issues in the development cycle that can jeopardize the security posture. You know and can show by example how to "test securely as well as test security " 

- You are a great collaborator who can be a valuable sparring partner with product managers to understand and refine customer's needs for security so that you define the right security designs for market segments. Engineering managers rely on your ability to steer security implementations within the product teams. 

- You are comfortable designing products that our customers will be running for years; comfortable providing guidance to LCM activities for existing customers to update hardware and software components to continuously stay secure. 

- You share the knowledge about security subjects; you explain why security practices exist and what they achieve in the long run. 

- You can translate security designs into engineering specifications, appraise implementation designs, conduct code reviews. This role with a strong hands-on component, not just a pure governance role. 

- You understand and can register, document, and communicate clearly risks and trade-offs between differen t project execution scenarios 

- You have had hands-on experience implementing security designs using modern programming language and frameworks, and you are able to coach product teams to increase their secure coding maturity e.g. by running threat modelling workshops with the engineering team. 

- You have vast experience with architecture roles with 3-5 years of experience specifically focusing on security. 

In addition, you have the following technical expertise: 

- Proven track record across at least two of the three domains: OT/IoT/embedded security, network security, cloud security 

- You are familiar with modern authentication and authorization frameworks (JWT, OpenID, SAML) and (REST) API security and protection approached 

- ISO 27001 and IEC 62443-4 understanding at a working level 

- Working knowledge with or excellent ability to apply the PKI and certificate lifecycle management at scale; also, with the vision how to implement this in OT/IoT deployment contexts 

- Solid network security understanding: firewall policy, micro-segmentation, DMZ design for IT/OT boundaries 

- Zero trust architecture principles 

- Secure SDLC and DevSecOps tools and practices (think about OWASP, SANS25, Snyk, Black Duck, etc) 

  

The following competence is desired: 

- OT/ICS protocols and architectures (such as BACnet Secure Connect, Modbus, DNP3, MQTT, AMQP) 

- Embedded device security for industrial PCs, systems-on-chip, and microcontrollers: secure boot, hardware security modules (HSMs), TPM, secure enclave concepts, firmware & data signing, encryption 

- Cloud security on at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) 

- Container and Kubernetes security 

- Secrets management and key management systems (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) 

- Priva's technical stack is C#/C++/.NET and Angular. Experience implementing production projects with this stack is preferred, but not required if you are able to learn it quickly (based on your vast experience) 

What we offer you 

  

💶 Excellent remuneration — competitive and aligned with experience. 

🌴 30 days holiday per year, with the option to buy 5 more at half price. 

🏦 Excellent pension contribution . 

🎓 Education budget of €1,000 per year. 

⏰ Flexible working hours . 

🍱 Onsite canteen (e.g., poke bowl for €2). 

🏋️ Free onsite gym . 

🎉 Vibrant, open culture .

title: Applied AI Engineer
description:
About Us 

Engelhart was founded in 2013 by BTG Pactual Group as a commodities trading company. Our business model is “asset light” and highly diversified – giving us the ability to adapt effectively and nimbly to changing market conditions. We have assembled successful multidisciplinary teams, leveraging advanced fundamental analysis with deep quantitative and weather research capabilities. Our activities are underpinned by strong risk management practices and by powerful technology and operational excellence. We have exceptional teams with diverse global backgrounds and decades of experience, and are driven by a highly collaborative culture, across products and competencies.

In 2024, Engelhart acquired Trailstone, a global energy trading and technology company. The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. The acquisition also expanded Engelhart’s capabilities into physical natural gas across North America, a critical fuel to support the energy transition.

Our talented and experienced individuals work together according to its four company values: Performance, Agility, Collaboration, Entrepreneurship .

About the Role 

As a member of the Tech Data, AI & UX team allocated to European & Asian Power Trading in Berlin, you will build the services, infrastructure, and AI & data platforms that power the business, enabling teams to improve their data-driven decisions and connect innovative products.

As part of this Joint Venture, the Applied AI Engineer will help to evolve ECTP’s AI & Agentic platforms – a strategic, firm-wide initiative led by the Tech Data, AI & UX team. The role provides hands-on exposure to the cutting edge of enterprise AI, working alongside experienced data engineer, architects and quant developers in a live, production-grade environment.

You will work closely with trading desk and Technology teams to build core agentic infrastructure, integrate tooling via AWS Lambda and MCP servers, develop agent skills, and configure knowledge bases across user, chat, agent, and application contexts. You will explore and evaluate open-source and proprietary connectors within the rapidly evolving LLM and Generative AI ecosystem, and help roll out individual productivity tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Claude Code. All solutions will be hosted securely within Engelhart’s internal network, with models deployed in a dedicated VPC and governed access to firm data, with a strong preference for AWS-native and Bedrock-based architectures.

This will be a full-time role, owning the following responsibilities :

- Collaborate with the trading desk to supercharge their research capabilities and data-driven insights by extending Engelhart's core AI and agentic platform to address new trading desk requirements.

- Assist in the set-up and configuration of core agentic AI infrastructure, including orchestration layers, agent runtimes, and supporting services, deployed securely within Engelhart’s AWS VPC.

- Build and maintain agent tooling integrations via AWS Lambda functions and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, enabling agents to interact with firm data, APIs, and internal systems.

- Develop agent skills and configure knowledge bases, including document stores, vector databases (e.g. Postgres with pgvector, AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases), and retrieval pipelines for user, chat, agent, and application contexts.

- Research, evaluate, and help integrate open-source and proprietary accelerators, connectors, and frameworks (e.g. LangChain, LlamaIndex, n8n, etc) into the platform, assessing fitness for purpose in a regulated, IP-sensitive environment.

- Support the deployment and end-user adoption of individual AI productivity tools, including Microsoft Copilot and Claude Code, ensuring secure configuration and appropriate access controls within Engelhart’s internal network.

- Contribute to technical documentation, architecture diagrams, and internal knowledge sharing on AI tooling, design decisions, and implementation patterns to support team learning and continuity.

- Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, and business stakeholders to iteratively test and improve agentic workflows, gathering feedback and translating it into technical improvements.

About You 

This person will be a technically minded and genuinely curious person who is excited about the transformative potential of AI and wants to go beyond surface-level tooling – you want to understand how things work and help build them. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, energised by fast-moving technology landscapes, and take pride in writing clean, well-structured code. You thrive in collaborative environments and are motivated by the opportunity to contribute to something that has real, visible impact within a live business setting.

The following education, experiences and skills are essential for application:

- Background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI, Data Science, or related technical undergraduate degree.

- A genuine passion for AI, Large Language Models, and Generative AI. Not just as a user, but with curiosity about how they work and how to build with them.

- Proficient in Python, with hands-on experience writing scripts, working with APIs, or building small applications – whether through coursework, personal projects, or hackathons.

- Familiarity with cloud concepts or services (preference for AWS), containerisation (Docker), or REST APIs – even if only at an introductory or project level.

- A proactive, self-directed learning style – able to research unfamiliar technologies, synthesise documentation, and form a view on trade-offs with limited guidance.

- Good communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues, and to work effectively in a small, fast-moving team.

- A collaborative, team-oriented mindset, with the confidence to contribute ideas, ask questions, and engage actively with engineers, data scientists, and business users.

- An organised approach to work, with attention to detail, a strong sense of ownership, and the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

- Comfortable working with ambiguity and rapid change, with the resilience to iterate quickly, adapt to new findings, and thrive in a technology landscape that evolves week to week.

In addition, the following criteria is not required, but highly desirable for this role:

- Foundational knowledge of energy trading markets, including core concepts like balancing mechanism operations, Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), and Virtual Power Plants (VPPs).

- Prior exposure to LLM frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar; experience with vector databases (e.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Chroma); or familiarity with AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, or equivalent managed AI services.

- Experience with version control (Git) and basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines or infrastructure-as-code (e.g. AWS CloudFormation, CDK).

- Understanding of prompt engineering techniques, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or multi-agent system design patterns.

- Participation in AI/ML hackathons, open-source contributions, personal projects involving LLMs or automation, or active engagement with the AI development community (e.g. Hugging Face, GitHub, LangChain forums).

- Portuguese as a second language.

What we offer 

- Competitive compensation and participation in Engelhart’s discretionary bonus plan.

- 28 days of annual holiday entitlement plus Berlin public holidays.

- €3,000 per year contribution to a private pension scheme on your behalf.

- €20 monthly subsidy towards BVG tickets.

- €25 monthly subsidy towards ClassPass membership.

- A subsidy for German language courses to help you immerse yourself in the local culture.

- A sociable working environment with an open, international culture.

We believe in inclusivity and are therefore dedicated to ensuring all employees – across gender identity, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, life experience, background and more – feel welcome and included in the company. We promote diversity because we believe it is essential to our ability to think holistically.

You'll report into the Product Engineering director within the BU, alongside other pods led by senior PMs, designers, or engineering managers.

Your impact at Brevo: 

- Gather client signals and usage data and translate them into clearly defined problems, then shape the pitch — appetite, solution, risks and no-gos — and defend it at the betting table.

- Act as the pod's sole design reference: frame the user experience, make interaction and interface decisions, and create prototypes in line with our Naos design system leveraging Claude or our in-house prototyping tool.

- Own the launch: run the beta programme, equip PMM for go-to-market, and get Sales, CSM and Support ready ahead of release.

- Be the pod's single point of contact for the wider BU — surfacing risks early, coordinating with peer Pod Leaders, and applying AI tools by default across discovery, prototyping and analysis.

- You can own an experience end-to-end: framing user problems, making interface/interaction decisions, and producing or validating prototypes (Figma and design-system literacy required).

- You're tech-credible: comfortable reading AI-generated code and partnering with a Lead Engineer on trade-offs — and you integrate AI tools by default into your day-to-day work, with a critical validation step on their outputs.

title: Senior Systems Engineer - Commissioning and Characterisation
description:
About the job 

Explore how a next-generation AI architecture behaves from rack scale to data centre scale. 

As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will investigate a novel AI computing architecture under demanding real-world workloads. You will work on problems where answers aren't readily known, turning curiosity into measurable evidence.

You will design experiments, benchmark representative AI workloads and explore how hardware components and software interact at scale. When behaviour is unexpected, you will turn this into new measurements.

Your work will help infrastructure engineers, architects and application specialists understand system behaviour, performance, scalability and reliability across the stack. You will also help develop tooling and automation to collect, analyse and visualise system metrics.

You do not need to be an AI expert. You will need strong judgement, curiosity and a clear preference for evidence over opinion. You will love this role if you are someone who takes initiative, questions assumptions and enjoys working in areas where the answers are not yet known.

The team and culture 

The System QA team is distributed across multiple locations. We work hard to stay connected and collaborate closely. Our daily team meetings feel more like a virtual coffee break than a formal status update with space to share ideas, ask questions, discuss discoveries and solve problems together.

We value trust, autonomy and openness, and we understand that great engineers don't all follow the same career path. What matters is the quality of your work, your curiosity, and your willingness to explore challenging problems.

You will have regular 1:1s with your people manager where you will have the opportunity to discuss things that matter to you. You will have dedicated time each week to focus on your CPD. The technical lead will provide direction and help set priorities, but everyone in the team is there to support each other.

One of our core principles is that we measure and report what we observe without trying to make results look better or worse than they are.

What we're looking for 

- Comfortable using Python to write tests, automate tasks, analyse data or develop practical engineering tools.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

- A curiosity-driven approach to investigating complex systems.

- Ability to explain technical findings clearly, using accurate and reproducible evidence.

- Confidence to work independently, take responsibility and collaborate across engineering teams.

- Experience in some of the following would be valuable: AI workloads and benchmarking, systems architecture, parallel and distributed computing, automation, containers or modern orchestration infrastructure

While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences from different industries. We actively welcome applications from engineers to the profession through a returnship or after a career break.

title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
About Uncovr

Uncovr is building AI-powered infrastructure for the future of surgery.

We work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, surgical video, clinical workflows, and healthcare technology. Our mission is to help surgical teams better understand, document, and improve surgical procedures by turning complex clinical data into structured, useful, and trustworthy insights.

We are a fast-moving startup working on technically ambitious problems with real-world clinical impact. As we expand our platform, we are looking for an AI Engineer to help build, test, and improve the AI systems that power our product.

About the Role

We are looking for an Senior AI Engineer to help develop reliable, accurate, and production-ready AI capabilities for complex clinical workflows.

In this role, you will work on AI system development, model integration, evaluation, testing, and production readiness. You will collaborate closely with product and engineering teams to turn product requirements into AI capabilities that are useful, reliable, and scalable.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who wants to build practical AI systems in production, not just experiment with models in isolation.

What You’ll Do

- Build, test, and improve AI systems that support Uncovr’s product.

- Work on AI workflows, model integration, evaluation, and production readiness.

- Integrate language models, multimodal models, and AI services into product and backend systems.

- Help improve AI system reliability, accuracy, latency, and robustness.

- Build and maintain evaluation workflows for AI outputs across product use cases.

- Test AI capabilities against real-world clinical and product scenarios.

- Help identify uncertainty, edge cases, failure modes, and inconsistent outputs.

- Support the development of validation layers that make AI outputs more reliable and useful.

- Collaborate with product and engineering teams to translate requirements into working AI capabilities.

- Contribute to logging, monitoring, error handling, documentation, and test coverage.

- Analyze feedback, corrections, and evaluation results to improve system behavior over time.

- Document AI workflows, assumptions, limitations, and known failure modes clearly.

What We’re Looking For

- Experience in AI engineering, applied ML, backend engineering, software engineering, or a related technical role.

- Strong Python skills and good software engineering fundamentals.

- Experience working with language models, multimodal models, AI APIs, or model-driven systems.

- Practical understanding of how to build, test, and debug AI-enabled product workflows.

- Ability to reason about AI system behavior, including errors, uncertainty, hallucinations, and failure modes.

- Experience integrating AI capabilities into backend services or product workflows.

- Familiarity with evaluation, testing, benchmarking, or quality checks for AI outputs.

- Ability to work closely with product, engineering, and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Strong attention to detail and comfort working with complex workflows.

- Clear communication skills and a willingness to document technical decisions, assumptions, and limitations.

- Comfort working in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.

Nice to Have

- Experience with multimodal AI systems, vision-language models, or AI systems using complex data.

- Experience with video understanding, computer vision, medical imaging, or healthcare AI.

- Familiarity with retrieval, structured outputs, evaluation pipelines, or AI observability.

- Experience building evaluation datasets, scoring workflows, or benchmark suites.

- Experience with human-in-the-loop systems or expert feedback workflows.

- Familiarity with MLOps, model deployment, or AI infrastructure.

- Experience working in regulated, high-trust, or safety-critical environments.

- Interest in surgery, clinical workflows, medical technology, and healthcare AI.

Who You Are

You are technical, curious, and motivated by building AI systems that work reliably in real-world settings.

You enjoy experimenting with AI systems, but you also care about testing, validation, edge cases, and production quality. You are interested in how AI behaves, where it fails, and how engineering can make it more accurate, transparent, and useful.

You are comfortable working closely with product teams, engineers, and domain experts. You communicate clearly, learn quickly, and want to contribute to technology with real clinical impact.

Why Join Uncovr

At Uncovr, you will help build and improve the AI systems behind a new generation of surgical intelligence tools.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to work on practical AI development, evaluation, and production readiness in a fast-moving healthcare technology company.

title: Senior Compliance Manager – Quality & Regulatory Affairs / QMB ISO 13485 (m/f/d)
description:
Intro Back problems are the most common reason for inability to work in Germany. 

Vivira has the solution: digital exercise therapy via app – always available, simple, effective, and reimbursed by health insurance. Behind every application permanently listed in the DiGA directory stands a robust quality management system. That is exactly why we are looking for you: As Senior Compliance Manager, you will take on the role of Quality Management Representative (QMB) according to ISO 13485 and keep our medical devices MDR-compliant – from the next audit to the inclusion of further products in the DiGA directory. 

Your responsibilities include As Senior Compliance Manager (m/f/d), you will be responsible for our quality management system and take on the role of Quality Management Representative according to ISO 13485. You report directly to our Team Lead Compliance and work closely with Engineering and Product. 

- QMS & Regulatory Affairs: You monitor compliance with DiGAV, MDR, ISO 13485, and ISO 27001, contribute to our BSI certification topics, and develop processes, SOPs, and Work Instructions pragmatically and based on risk. 

- Technical Documentation: You create and maintain the Technical Documentation according to MDR (DHF/DMR) for our three medical devices – one app listed in the DiGA directory and two CE-marked products in DiGA studies. 

- Audits: You prepare and follow up on external audits with the notified body, and plan and conduct internal audits. Your first milestone: the ISO 13485 recertification audit in February 2027 – with a stable system, complete documentation, and a planned handover by your predecessor. 

- Releases & Post-Market Surveillance: You review and approve release documentation and are responsible for post-market surveillance of our products. 

- Supplier Management: You evaluate and monitor our software providers (e.g. Atlassian, HubSpot, Google) according to criticality. 

- Regulatory Radar: You evaluate regulatory changes monthly and derive concrete measures. 

- Interface within the Company: You are the primary contact for regulatory questions across all departments – from Doctor Success to Patient Success –, train colleagues, and proactively gather input. 

Whether the role of PRRC (Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance) becomes part of the function will be discussed together during the selection process – depending on your qualification and a clear agreement on responsibilities. 

The biggest challenge? Making regulatory requirements understandable across the company – explaining why something is necessary rather than just distributing guidelines – and actively engaging colleagues both in the office and remotely. 

What you should bring - You have at least three years of relevant experience in the medical device field and know MDR and ISO 13485 from practical experience. You want to bring your QM/RA experience into a dedicated QMB role – or already bring it with you. 

- You have prepared, accompanied, and followed up on audits. Having independently managed an audit is a plus – as is experience with internal audits. 

- You bring genuine technical understanding: You know how software development works (frontend vs. backend, releases, tickets) without needing to code yourself. A background in hardware or implants is welcome if your tech affinity is right. 

- You are ready to assume the QMB role according to ISO 13485. 

- You work in a structured, thorough, and independent manner, actively approach colleagues, and follow up when input is missing. You can say "No, that won't work" – while simultaneously finding pragmatic, risk-based solutions that Engineering and Product can work with. 

- You have very good German skills (at least C1) to reliably understand and communicate German DiGA regulations, and very good English skills for collaborating with our engineering team. 

- A plus, but not a requirement: Experience with DiGA or Digital Health, SaMD (Software as a Medical Device), ISO 27001 / ISMS or BSI certifications, as well as knowledge of Confluence, Jira, or Matrix Requirements. 

What to expect at Vivira - Ownership: You independently design the QMS – your own processes, high freedom, short decision-making paths. 

- Career Leap: Your own QMB responsibility covering a broad spectrum including MDR, DiGA, ISO 13485, ISO 27001, and BSI – built on an established system with a planned handover. 

- Workplace: Hybrid in Berlin with 1–2 days per week in the office. Travel occurs only occasionally (under 10%). 

- Working Abroad: Up to one month per year, you can work from within the EU, EEA, Switzerland, Israel, or the UK. 

- Recharge: 30 vacation days for true breaks. 

- Health: Our app for your own back health. 

- Securing the Future: Increased employer contribution to the company pension scheme. 

- Corporate Benefits: Exclusive benefits for shopping, tech, and more. 

- Referral Bonus: Every successful recommendation from your network is rewarded. 

- Highlights: Multiple company and team events per year – and a dedicated team.

- Define and own evaluation frameworks for generative outputs, including automated metrics, LLM-as-judge approaches, human evaluation protocols, hallucination detection, and drift monitoring.

- Evaluations: Strong experience defining and running evaluation pipelines for generative AI — automated scoring, human evaluation design, hallucination mitigation, and drift monitoring. LLM-as-judge patterns are a plus.

- LLMs & GenAI: Demonstrated experience with foundation models and GenAI providers (AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta). Comfortable with fine-tuning, instruction tuning, and prompt engineering at scale.

- Traditional NLP: Solid grounding in classical NLP techniques (NER, text classification, intent detection, topic modelling) and good judgement on when to apply them alongside or instead of LLMs.

- AWS Bedrock: Hands-on experience with Amazon Bedrock: foundation model APIs, Bedrock Agents, Knowledge Bases, and Guardrails. Experience with Bedrock Model Evaluation is a plus.

- AWS Ecosystem: Proficiency with SageMaker, Lambda, ECS/EKS, S3, OpenSearch, IAM, CloudWatch, and VPC networking.

- MLOps & CI/CD: Familiarity with model registries, CI/CD for ML, feature stores, canary deployments, monitoring, and rollback.

- IaC: Experience with Terraform or AWS CDK for reproducible infrastructure provisioning.

- Python: Production-quality Python: packaging, testing (pytest), type hints, async programming, and clean ML pipeline abstractions.

- ML Frameworks: Familiarity with traditional ML frameworks and fine-tuning workflows.

- Experiment Tracking: Experience with Langfuse, Arize or Langsmith, or equivalent for tracking runs, metrics, and artefacts.

- Ability to translate ambiguous business goals into concrete technical solutions and communicate tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders.

- Strong collaborative instincts — comfortable working across engineering, product, and data teams.

- A rigorous, evidence-driven mindset: you ship with confidence because you measure, test, and monitor thoroughly.

Education: 

- A Master’s degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science with a preference for specialization in the NLP domain.

Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. Hiring: VIN Decode Engineer, Data Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Founding Engineer (dealer platform). TypeScript, Postgres, Cloudflare Workers. Full descriptions and apply: https://cardog.app/careers

title: Ingénieur PS Zero Trust / SASE (Cloudflare One)
description:
À propos de Brixio

Brixio est un partenaire spécialiste de Cloudflare : intégration, services professionnels et services managés sur l'ensemble de la plateforme, de la sécurité applicative au SASE. Brixio est partenaire Cloudflare certifié ASDP et fait partie depuis juillet 2026 du groupe Equans (groupe Bouygues), 18,7 Md€ de chiffre d'affaires et environ 85 000 personnes.

L'équipe compte une trentaine d'ingénieurs répartis entre Paris, Dubaï et un centre de production à Casablanca. Les clients sont des grands comptes et des ETI en France, en Europe et au Moyen-Orient, ainsi que les entités du groupe Equans.

La mission

L'ingénieur PS Zero Trust / SASE déploie Cloudflare One chez les clients français de Brixio, du cadrage technique à la mise en production. Il devient la référence opérationnelle Zero Trust de l'équipe France et prend en charge les projets SASE dès son arrivée, notamment le déploiement interne de Cloudflare One chez Brixio et l'accès distant sécurisé aux sites industriels du groupe Equans.

Il travaille avec le Delivery Manager France, qui pilote le planning, le budget et la relation projet, et avec l'architecte principal, référent technique de l'équipe.

Responsabilités

- Cadrage : animer les ateliers techniques avec les équipes réseau, sécurité et poste de travail du client, puis rédiger le design détaillé (architecture d'accès, politiques, plan de migration).
- Déploiement Cloudflare One : Access (ZTNA), Gateway (SWG et filtrage DNS), client WARP, Tunnel, CASB, DLP, isolation de navigation (RBI), et selon les projets Magic WAN, Magic Firewall et Email Security.
- Migrations : remplacer les VPN par du ZTNA et les proxies existants par Gateway, sans rupture de service pour les utilisateurs.
- Intégrations : fournisseurs d'identité (Entra ID, Okta) en SAML, OIDC et SCIM, contrôles de posture (Intune, EDR), remontée des logs vers le SIEM du client.
- OT et industrie : sécuriser l'accès distant des prestataires et techniciens aux équipements industriels et techniques.
- Sécurité des usages IA : appliquer les contrôles Cloudflare One aux usages de l'IA (détection du shadow AI, DLP sur les prompts, gouvernance des applications IA).
- Livraison et passation : documentation (HLD, LLD, runbooks), recette avec le client, passation au support et au MSP de Casablanca.
- Rigueur projet : travailler dans le périmètre signé, signaler au Delivery Manager toute demande hors périmètre avant de la traiter, et saisir son temps chaque semaine dans Brixio One.
- Industrialisation : contribuer aux modèles de déploiement réutilisables (configurations types, Terraform, playbooks) pour accélérer les projets suivants.

Requirements 

Profil indispensable

Le poste demande d'être opérationnel sur le SASE dès les premières semaines. Sans expérience SASE en production, la candidature ne sera pas retenue.

- SASE en production : au moins 2 ans de déploiements Zero Trust / SASE chez des clients, sur Cloudflare One, Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA), Netskope, Palo Alto Prisma Access, Cato Networks ou Fortinet SASE.
- Expérience : 3 à 6 ans en sécurité réseau, intégration ou services professionnels.
- Fondamentaux réseau : TCP/IP, DNS, TLS et PKI, routage, VPN IPsec, proxies, pare-feu.
- Identité : SSO en SAML et OIDC, provisioning SCIM, Entra ID ou Okta.
- Poste de travail : déploiement d'agents à grande échelle, MDM et contrôles de posture.
- Relation client : capacité à animer seul un atelier technique et à rédiger une documentation claire.
- Langues : français courant, anglais professionnel (équipe internationale).
- Mobilité : déplacements réguliers chez les clients en France, ponctuellement en Europe.
Atouts

- Expérience directe de Cloudflare One, ou certification Cloudflare (sinon, à obtenir dans les 90 jours suivant l'arrivée).
- Automatisation : Terraform, API, scripts Python.
- Connaissance des environnements OT et industriels.
- Connaissance des exigences NIS2 et DORA.
- Intérêt pour l'IA et pour la plateforme développeurs de Cloudflare (AI Gateway, Workers).
Évolution et ce que Brixio offre

Le poste démarre sur le SASE mais ne s'y limite pas. Il s'ouvre ensuite aux autres produits Cloudflare (sécurité applicative, API Shield, Workers, IA), selon la progression et l'intérêt de la personne. La sécurité de l'IA s'appuie largement sur Cloudflare One, ce qui fait de ce poste une porte d'entrée naturelle vers les projets IA de Brixio.

- Rémunération fixe selon profil, plus une part variable liée à des objectifs projet (qualité, respect des délais, saisie des temps).
- Certifications Cloudflare prises en charge.
- Projets variés chez des grands comptes, des ETI et les entités d'un groupe international.
- Une équipe à taille humaine, avec la solidité du groupe Equans.
Processus de recrutement

- Entretien de présentation avec le cabinet de recrutement.
- Entretien technique avec l'architecte principal, avec un cas pratique SASE (migration VPN vers ZTNA).

title: Staff Software Engineer, Enterprise Platform
description:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord's Enterprise Technology org is building a software engineering discipline from the ground up, and this is the founding engineering hire. There is no Enterprise Platform team yet. You will not be maintaining a status quo or joining an existing backlog: you will define the discipline, set the technical foundation, and build the platform that lets the internal systems enabling Discordians scale with the company.

Discord's mission is to cultivate belonging, and doing that at scale requires internal systems that move as fast as the product itself. The mission of this role is to turn our enterprise infrastructure into self-service software. Your job is to replace manual consoles and tickets with a platform of reusable primitives, building blocks like "provision a device" or "push an IAM policy or app integration through code," exposed through clean APIs and self-service portals. As a code-forward Staff engineer, you will design abstractions that hide the messy reality of Okta, Jamf, and Terraform (our identity, device management, and infrastructure-as-code tools) behind interfaces people actually want to use, operating with a platform-as-a-product mindset.

What You'll Do 

- Manage the device fleet as code: Move device configuration off consoles and into versioned, API-driven infrastructure for endpoint management and hardware provisioning.

- Automate the identity layer: Manage identity systems and their connections to downstream apps as code, from SSO and SCIM integrations to account workflows, so changes ship through version control and CI/CD instead of an admin console.

- Own app delivery and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Build deployment pipelines and provisioning patterns that let internal systems be built and changed safely, establishing CI/CD standards.

- Build the self-service layer: Design and ship the APIs, CLIs, and portals that compose primitives into paved paths, like a new hire's first day, where software access and group memberships land in one automated, auditable flow.

- Set the foundation: Define the technical direction and architecture for the discipline, writing the RFCs and documentation that future hires will build on.

What You Should Have 

- 6+ years building and operating production software and systems at a technology company, with a track record of owning ambiguous projects end to end.

- Strong software engineering fundamentals. You write production code (we lean on Python, TypeScript and Rust), and design, test, and ship it. This is not a systems admin role.

- Deep, hands-on IAM experience (SSO, SCIM, OAuth/OIDC, RBAC) and fluency with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD.

- Experience treating endpoint and fleet management as an API-driven engineering surface at scale.

- A platform-as-a-product mindset. You have built self-service tooling that people chose to adopt.

- Comfort with ambiguity and a founder's temperament; energized by building from scratch.

Bonus Points 

- Hands-on experience with Okta, Jamf, or Intune.

- Experience with identity and access governance for non-human, workload, or AI-agent principals.

- Background at a high-growth consumer tech company with a highly technical employee base.

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. title: Robot Learning Engineer, Human Motion Data (m/f/d)
description:
About EASE

EASE builds active, AI-powered exoskeletons for logistics and manufacturing. As a TUM spin-off, we have just started series production, and paid pilots with well-known logistics companies have led to first purchase orders. Our goal: move every parcel better, manually with an exoskeleton or autonomously with a robot.

The role

Our exoskeletons are deployed in real warehouses and production plants and capture what video-only datasets miss: body pose, joint kinematics, interaction torques, vision, and hand forces from real human work. Your job is to turn that data into skills our humanoid can actually perform, so that human workers and robots can work side by side on the same tasks.

What you'll do

- Map human motion onto humanoid kinematics and close the embodiment gap

- Train manipulation and whole-body policies with imitation and reinforcement learning

- Evaluate in Isaac Lab or MuJoCo and on our in-house humanoid, and measure the value of our data

- Define what data training needs and help build our training setup, including GPU compute

- Turn new research on robot foundation models and VLAs into prototypes

What you bring

- Master's or PhD in robotics, CS, ML or similar, with hands-on experience from industry or research

- Imitation or reinforcement learning on real robots (e.g. Diffusion Policy, ACT, PPO)

- Strong Python and PyTorch; C++ is a plus

- Physics simulation and sim-to-real transfer

- Solid kinematics, dynamics and control

Nice to have

- Learning from human data (egocentric video, motion capture, retargeting)

- Humanoids, legged robots or exoskeletons; publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA or NeurIPS

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. What you have built matters more than a perfect match.

What we offer

- Data almost nobody else has, from a product in series deployment

- Our own humanoid and the chance to build Physical AI at EASE from the ground up

- Competitive salary plus virtual stock options (VSOP)

- Flexible hours, hybrid in Munich, mobility benefit

- Budget for conferences and further training

How to apply

Send your CV with links to GitHub, papers or robot videos.

Martin Fleischer, CEO & Co-Founder

EASE is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants need a valid work permit for the EU.

description:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone. 

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London or Remote (UK) | 💰 £79,000 - £93,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits 

🌟 About the team: 

Our Borrowing (lending) business is growing rapidly across both existing products and with the planned launch of new initiatives. As our lending portfolio grows, our second line of defence Credit Model Validation team is growing with it - and we’re looking for a Credit Model Validation Manager to join us!

Our Credit Model Validation team is crucial in providing independent oversight and challenge to our model development teams in the first line of defence to help Monzo grow safely and ensure that the models we use deliver good outcomes for our customers. We’re looking for someone (maybe you?!) to join our validation squad and provide expert independent validation and oversight across our suite of credit models, covering critical business disciplines such as credit strategy and impairment.

You’ll have a particular focus on models used for customer-level decisioning and defining our credit strategies - such as underwriting scorecards, origination PD models and Net Present Value (NPV) / unit economics models - across all our lending products.

Strong data and analytical skills are a must, as is deep expertise in credit risk modelling. You’ll have hands-on experience in either model validation or model development within a financial services environment, including practical experience using Python to develop, validate or analyse machine learning and statistical models. . In-depth knowledge of credit decisioning models would be a strong plus. 

🔑 You’ll play a key role by… 

- Leading hands-on independent validation of models used for credit decisioning within our Borrowing strategies - covering a range of machine learning, decision science and NPV models. You will be ensuring that models are fit for purpose, appropriately governed, explainable and performing as expected

- Supporting oversight and validation of broader credit risk models, including IFRS9, stress testing and economic response models

- Developing deep understanding of Monzo’s credit models, and using this to provide impactful input and challenge to model developers to improve our modelling capabilities

- Reviewing ongoing model performance monitoring to ensure our lending models perform within our risk thresholds, and providing support to our first line of defence teams when action is required

- Performing statistical analyses to independently assess model performance, including developing challenger models where appropriate to test model assumptions and strengthen validation conclusions

- Improving our Model Risk Framework, including overseeing our policies, standards and procedures to help embed best practice across the business. This means making sure we follow up-to-date regulatory guidelines, and adapt our processes to make sure they remain relevant as modelling techniques evolve

- Writing clear and impactful model validation reports, and presenting the findings and actions in relevant committees

- Partnering with colleagues in the first line of defence credit strategy and modelling teams - and wider risk teams across Monzo - to support the embedding of our model risk framework and establishing consistent validation standards across the organisation

- Embracing new and innovative technology, including leading the adoption of AI tools to enhance our model validation approach

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if… 

- Have a strong background and practical experience in credit model development and/or validation - in particular with exposure to machine learning or statistical models used in credit decisioning, such as decision science scorecards, origination / underwriting PD models, and NPV / unit economics modelling

- Are data driven, with strong analytical skills and deep understanding of statistical techniques for credit and model risk. Being able to get hands on with data is critical - so strong SQL and Python skills are essential, and experience with data visualisation tools such as Tableau, Looker or similar is a plus!

- Understand how models are used in real-time decisioning and lending strategies, and how to balance commercial and risk outcomes

- Have strong written and verbal communication skills, and are able to articulate problems and solutions using clear and simple language. This is particularly important for breaking down complex issues and priorities to non-experts

- Have a track record of building and maintaining trusting relationships with stakeholders at all levels, and can provide effective and respectful challenge

- Are impact-driven, and proactive in identifying issues and opportunities to improve outcomes for both our customers and our business

- Are passionate about technology, and what we’re doing here at Monzo excites you!

Our technology stack 

We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies (note we do not expect applicants to have prior experience of all them):

- Google Cloud Platform for all of our analytics infrastructure

- dbt and BigQuery SQL for our data modelling and warehousing

- Python for data science and machine learning

- Go to write our application code

- AWS for most of our backend infrastructure

The interview process: 

Our interview process usually involves up to four main stages via Google Hangouts: 

- An initial call with our recruiter

- A call with our Senior Model Validation Manager, the hiring manager for the role 

- A role-specific call with colleagues from our credit modelling teams. We’ll share a short case study in advance, but you won’t need to submit a written response; we’ll use it to guide the discussion during the interview.

- A behavioural interview 

🙌 What’s in it for you 

- 💰 £79,000 - £93,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance benefits.

- 📍 This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

- ⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

- 📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

- 🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given MacBooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.

- ➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits .
